Write the README-style usage and two or three real call sites before the types, then derive the type sketch from them. The usage is the spec. The two must agree, so reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.\\n- Data structures first. Get the core types right and the code becomes obvious. Trace each dominant access pattern through the proposed structure. If the answer is \\\"we'll add a map / index / cache later,\\\" the structure is wrong.\\n- Interface depth. Compare the capability hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface that pulls complexity into the callee, even when the implementation becomes less simple. Do not put transport or wire types on the public API. Parse into domain types behind the interface.\\n- Shared state: if two actors might both write, ask \\\"what happens?\\\" If the answer isn't \\\"nothing,\\\" default to per-actor state with a merge at the read boundary, per the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill.\\n- Make boundaries visible. `not implemented` errors for bodies, `// TODO` pseudocode for tricky logic, doc comments stating intent and invariants. A reader should trace data from input to output by reading types and signatures alone.\\n- Encode invariants in types: hard-to-misuse types > runtime checks > prose comments, per the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.\\n- Validate at boundaries, trust types inside, per the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. Business logic as pure functions. The shell stays thin.\\n- Single source of truth per invariant. Derive instead of sync.\\n- Idempotent state transitions where applicable, per the **make-operations-idempotent** principle skill. Ask what happens if the operation runs twice or crashes halfway.\\n- Short call chains. If tracing the flow needs more than three files, flatten the hierarchy, per the **laziness-protocol** and **minimize-reader-load** principle skills.\\n\\nWith observed independent workers, you are one of the parallel runners. Different models are a goal, not an assumed fact. Record requested and observed models; unknown or identical observed models do not establish diversity. In a sequential fallback, you are producing one explicitly labelled sequential alternative. Produce the best design your model can make. Don't hedge against the others. Differences between candidates are the signal used to pick a base and graft. Converging on a safe-looking middle defeats the exploration.\\n# Rationale template\\n\\nThe prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate. Replace the italic notes with actual content.\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\n*One paragraph. What we're trying to do, and what about the existing system or constraints makes the shape non-obvious. If [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) surfaced constraints the design must honor (existing types to interop with, callers we can't break, invariants that crossed our boundary), name them here so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.*\\n\\n## Usage (caller's view)\\n\\n*Write this first, before the type sketch. Show the README or quickstart the consumer reads, plus two or three realistic call sites in their own code. What they import, what they call, what comes back. The type sketch in [Shape](#shape) is derived from this. The two must agree. When they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse. The caller's experience is the spec. The types serve it.*\\n\\n## Shape\\n\\n*The recommended architecture. Data structures first. Then how data flows through the signatures. Name the load-bearing decisions. State which invariants are encoded in types, where validation lives, and what the system deliberately does not do. Judge interface depth explicitly. State what complexity the public surface hides, what remains exposed to callers, and why the interface is no larger than needed. Cite the principle behind each decision (e.g., `per boundary-discipline`). Don't restate it.*\\n\\n## Synthesis decision\\n\\n*Filled in by [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.*\\n\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\n\\n*One bullet per tradeoff the chosen shape makes. Form: \\\"we accept X in exchange for Y.\\\" Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.*\\n\\n## Alternatives considered\\n\\n*Required. Name at least one concrete alternative shape, with one line on why it lost. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone. Name the complexity it exposes to callers and the complexity it hides. Two or three alternatives belong here when the design space had real contenders. One is fine when the constraints forced the answer, with the conclusion phrased as \\\"this was the only viable shape because...\\\" Avoid listing flavors of the same shape. This section covers design alternatives the chosen shape considered and rejected, not other runner candidates.*\\n\\n## Open questions and risks\\n\\n*Things you noticed during the sketch that the human needs to weigh in on, and risks worth flagging before implementation starts. Phrase as questions, not assertions, so the human's answer is the resolution rather than a comment.*\\n\\n## Next implementation step\\n\\n*The first thing to build against the sketch. One sentence. What you'd start writing immediately after synthesis (or after Phase D sign-off, if a checkpoint was opted into).*\\n# Design red flags\\n\\nScreen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.\\n\\n## Shallow module\\n\\nA shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.\\n\\nDo not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.\\n\\nLook for these signs:\\n\\n- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.\\n- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.\\n- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.\\n\\n## Information leakage\\n\\nInformation leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.\\n\\nPublic re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.\\n\\n## Temporal decomposition\\n\\nTemporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.\\n\\nGroup code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.\\n\\n## Pass-through method\\n\\nA pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.\\n\\nRemove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.\\n\\n## Split ownership\\n\\nMore than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can't see the others, so their rules diverge.\\n\\nGive each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.\\n\\n## Two ways to do one task\\n\\nThe design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.\\n\\nKeep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.\\n\\n## Importable internals\\n\\nA caller can import a module's internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.\\n\\nMake internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.\\n\\n## Hand-synced list\\n\\nTwo or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.\\n\\nKeep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can't be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.\\n---\\nname: principle-exhaust-the-design-space\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Exhaust the Design Space\\n\\nWhen a novel interaction or architectural decision has no established precedent, explore several concrete alternatives before implementation. Building the wrong thing costs more than exploring three options.\\n\\n**The rule.** When the right answer is not obvious, build 2-3 competing prototypes or sketches. Compare them side by side. Only then commit. Design it twice is this rule by another name. A second flavor of the first shape does not count.\\n\\n**When it applies:**\\n- Novel UI interactions (no prior art in the codebase)\\n- Architectural choices with multiple viable approaches\\n- Product design decisions where user experience depends on feel, not logic\\n\\n**When it doesn't:**\\n- Mechanical implementation where the pattern is established\\n- Bug fixes or refactors with a clear target state\\n- Changes where constraints dictate a single viable approach\\n\\n## Capability and authorization limits\\n\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before prototype writes or execution. Use available tools only within the authorized task and host permissions. Choosing an approach after comparison does not authorize a version-control commit, publication or external write.\\n\\nWhen execution is unavailable, compare distinct sketches or proposals and label them untested. State which runtime behavior or interaction feel remains unverified. If writes are unavailable, present sketches in the response. If the decision requires construction or evaluation that cannot be performed, report that step as blocked and name the missing capability. Claim successful execution only from observed results.\\n\\nPreserve the invocation metadata above. Its presence does not establish that the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-laziness-protocol\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Laziness Protocol\\n\\nAim for the most result with the least code and complexity.\\n\\n- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.\\n- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.\\n- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.\\n- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat \\\"elegant\\\" boilerplate.\\n- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.\\n- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.\\n\\n**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.\\n\\n## Capability limits\\n\\nApply this principle within the authorized task. Follow [session capability checks](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before claiming file reads, edits or verification. When writes or execution are unavailable, label the read-only proposal as reduced capability and state the missing checks. If required source is unavailable, state that the refactor cannot be assessed. Structural validation does not prove runtime behavior.\\n---\\nname: principle-redesign-from-first-principles\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Redesign From First Principles\\n\\nWhen integrating a change, don't bolt it onto the existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been there from the start.\\n\\n- Read all affected files and understand the current design\\n- Ask: \\\"if we were writing this from scratch with this new requirement, what would we build?\\\"\\n- Propagate the change through every reference: types, docs, examples, rationale sections\\n- Think about the whole redesign, then deliver it incrementally\\n\\nThis is the method for preserving option value when integrating changes into an existing design.\\n\\n## Capability and permission boundaries\\n\\nUse the [session capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before reading source, editing files or running checks. Apply the redesign within the authorized task. Propagating references does not grant permission to change unrelated files or perform external actions.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, provide a concrete redesign and incremental sequence as reduced capability. State which edits and checks were not performed. If affected source or design context is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep any redesign provisional. Claim implementation or verification only after observing the authorized operation.\\n---\\nname: show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. Validate every argument before any write.\\nif [ -z \\\"$1\\\" ]; then\\n    printf 'error: an explicit owned output path is required\\\\n' >&2\\n    exit 1\\nfi\\nfor value in \\\"$@\\\"; do\\n    case \\\"$value\\\" in\\n        *$'\\\\t'*|*$'\\\\n'*|*$'\\\\r'*)\\n            printf 'error: tabs, newlines and carriage returns are not allowed\\\\n' >&2\\n            exit 1\\n            ;;\\n    esac\\ndone\\nlogfile=\\\"$1\\\"\\nshift\\n\\nlogdir=\\\"$(dirname \\\"$logfile\\\")\\\"\\nif [ -n \\\"$logdir\\\" ] && [ \\\"$logdir\\\" != \\\".\\\" ] && [ ! -d \\\"$logdir\\\" ]; then\\n\\tmkdir -p \\\"$logdir\\\"\\nfi\\n\\n# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log\\n# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.\\nif [ ! -s \\\"$logfile\\\" ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'ts\\\\tphase\\\\tdecision\\\\twhy\\\\tevidence\\\\tresult\\\\n' >> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\nfi\\n\\nts=\\\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\\\"\\n# Record separators were rejected above. Prefix any cell\\n# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)\\n# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in\\n# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,\\n# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer\\n# opens the file.\\nclean() {\\n\\tlocal v\\n\\tv=\\\"$1\\\"\\n\\tcase \\\"$v\\\" in\\n\\t\\t=*|+*|-*|@*) printf \\\"'%s\\\" \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\t\\t*) printf '%s' \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\tesac\\n}\\nprintf '%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\n' \\\\\\n\\t\\\"$ts\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$1\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$2\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$3\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$4\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$5\\\")\\\" \\\\\\n\\t>> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\n#!/usr/bin/env bun\\nimport fs from \\\"node:fs\\\";\\nimport process from \\\"node:process\\\";\\nimport path from \\\"node:path\\\";\\n\\nconst RULE =\\n\\t\\\"Tests alone are not sufficient verification. Full verification requires unit evidence, live evidence, and performance evidence or justified non-applicability.\\\";\\nconst SUB_BLOCKS = [\\n\\t\\\"Depends on.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Files.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Build.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"You see.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, unit.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, live.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, perf.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Review gate.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Merge.\\\",\\n];\\nconst PROGRAM_H3 = [\\\"Arm the program\\\", \\\"Spawn owners\\\", \\\"PR mechanics\\\", \\\"Verdict and merge\\\", \\\"Boot recipe\\\"];\\nconst PROGRAM_MARKERS = [\\\"baseline\\\", \\\"status message\\\"];\\nconst HOW_TO_READ_MARKERS = [\\n\\t\\\"One box is one unit of work\\\",\\n\\t\\\"names the evidence\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Check a box only when its evidence exists\\\",\\n\\t\\\"playbooks/\\\",\\n\\tRULE,\\n];\\nconst PERF_ITEMS = [\\\"Metric.\\\", \\\"Probe.\\\", \\\"Baseline.\\\", \\\"Rule.\\\"];\\nconst BOX = /^\\\\s*- \\\\[[ x]\\\\] (.*)$/;\\n\\nconst file = process.argv[2];\\nif (!file || process.argv.length !== 3) {\\n\\tconsole.error(\\\"Usage: bun --no-install check-plan.mjs <pstack-plan.md>\\\");\\n\\tprocess.exit(2);\\n}\\n\\nlet raw;\\ntry { raw = fs.readFileSync(file, \\\"utf8\\\").split(/\\\\r?\\\\n/); }\\ncatch (error) { console.error(`${file}: cannot read plan (${error.code})`); process.exit(2); }\\nconst problems = [];\\nconst fail = (line, message) => problems.push(`${file}:${line}: ${message}`);\\n\\nlet start = 0;\\nif (raw[0] === \\\"---\\\") {\\n\\tstart = raw.indexOf(\\\"---\\\", 1) + 1;\\n}\\n\\nconst lines = [];\\nlet fence = false;\\nfor (let i = start; i < raw.length; i++) {\\n\\tconst text = raw[i];\\n\\tconst n = i + 1;\\n\\tif (/^```/.test(text)) fence = !fence;\\n\\tlines.push({ n, text, code: fence });\\n\\tif (fence) continue;\\n\\tconst prose = text\\n\\t\\t.replace(/`[^`]*`/g, \\\"`\\\")\\n\\t\\t.replace(/!\\\\[[^\\\\]]*\\\\]\\\\([^)]*\\\\)/g, \\\"\\\")\\n\\t\\t.replace(/\\\\]\\\\([^)]*\\\\)/g, \\\"]\\\");\\n\\tif (/[\\\\u2013\\\\u2014]/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"long dash\\\");\\n\\tif (/[\\\\u2018\\\\u2019\\\\u201c\\\\u201d]/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"curly quote\\\");\\n\\tif (/: \\\\S/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"mid-sentence colon\\\");\\n}\\n\\nconst h2 = (l) => (!l.code && l.text.startsWith(\\\"## \\\") ? l.text.slice(3).trim() : null);\\nconst sections = [];\\nfor (const l of lines) {\\n\\tconst title = h2(l);\\n\\tif (title !== null) sections.push({ title, n: l.n, body: [] });\\n\\telse if (sections.length) sections.at(-1).body.push(l);\\n}\\nconst find = (title) => sections.find((s) => s.title === title);\\nconst bodyText = (s) => s.body.map((l) => l.text).join(\\\"\\\\n\\\");\\nconst boxes = (ls) => ls.filter((l) => !l.code && BOX.test(l.text)).map((l) => ({ n: l.n, text: l.text.match(BOX)[1] }));\\n// This is a pstack template validator. It never edits a plan or validates\\n// implementation plans owned by another workflow.\\nif (!find(\\\"How to read this\\\") || !find(\\\"Program checklist\\\")) {\\n\\tconsole.error(`${file}:1: not a pstack multi-phase plan; leave other workflow plans unchanged`);\\n\\tprocess.exit(1);\\n}\\nconst capabilities = find(\\\"Capabilities\\\");\\nconst capabilityText = capabilities ? bodyText(capabilities) : \\\"\\\";\\nconst declared = {};\\nfor (const name of [\\\"Independent workers\\\", \\\"Live control\\\", \\\"Scheduling\\\", \\\"Remote\\\", \\\"Model selection\\\"]) {\\n\\tconst line = capabilities?.body.find((l) => !l.code && l.text.startsWith(`${name} `));\\n\\tconst match = line?.text.match(/^(.*?) (available|unavailable)\\\\. Evidence `([^`<>]+)`\\\\./);\\n\\tif (!match) fail(line?.n ?? 1, `${name}: missing capability evidence and available/unavailable declaration`);\\n\\telse declared[name] = { available: match[2] === \\\"available\\\", text: line.text, n: line.n };\\n}\\nconst capacity = Number(declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.text.match(/Capacity (\\\\d+)\\\\./)?.[1] ?? 0);\\nif (declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.available && capacity < 1) fail(declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"].n, \\\"available independent workers require observed capacity\\\");\\nfor (const [name, pattern] of [[\\\"Scheduling\\\", /\\\\/loop\\\\s|scheduled audit/i], [\\\"Remote\\\", /cloud VM|remote creation/i], [\\\"Model selection\\\", /Ten lanes on `|explicit model|grok-4/i]]) {\\n\\tfor (const line of lines) if (!line.code && pattern.test(line.text) && !declared[name]?.available) fail(line.n, `${name} claim lacks available capability evidence`);\\n}\\n\\nconst h1 = lines.findIndex((l) => !l.code && l.text.startsWith(\\\"# \\\"));\\nif (h1 === -1) fail(1, \\\"no H1 title\\\");\\nconst howToRead = find(\\\"How to read this\\\");\\nif (!howToRead) fail(1, 'no \\\"## How to read this\\\" Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. Validate every argument before any write.\\nif [ -z \\\"$1\\\" ]; then\\n    printf 'error: an explicit owned output path is required\\\\n' >&2\\n    exit 1\\nfi\\nfor value in \\\"$@\\\"; do\\n    case \\\"$value\\\" in\\n        *$'\\\\t'*|*$'\\\\n'*|*$'\\\\r'*)\\n            printf 'error: tabs, newlines and carriage returns are not allowed\\\\n' >&2\\n            exit 1\\n            ;;\\n    esac\\ndone\\nlogfile=\\\"$1\\\"\\nshift\\n\\nlogdir=\\\"$(dirname \\\"$logfile\\\")\\\"\\nif [ -n \\\"$logdir\\\" ] && [ \\\"$logdir\\\" != \\\".\\\" ] && [ ! -d \\\"$logdir\\\" ]; then\\n\\tmkdir -p \\\"$logdir\\\"\\nfi\\n\\n# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log\\n# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.\\nif [ ! -s \\\"$logfile\\\" ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'ts\\\\tphase\\\\tdecision\\\\twhy\\\\tevidence\\\\tresult\\\\n' >> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\nfi\\n\\nts=\\\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\\\"\\n# Record separators were rejected above. Prefix any cell\\n# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)\\n# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in\\n# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,\\n# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer\\n# opens the file.\\nclean() {\\n\\tlocal v\\n\\tv=\\\"$1\\\"\\n\\tcase \\\"$v\\\" in\\n\\t\\t=*|+*|-*|@*) printf \\\"'%s\\\" \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\t\\t*) printf '%s' \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\tesac\\n}\\nprintf '%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\n' \\\\\\n\\t\\\"$ts\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$1\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$2\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$3\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$4\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$5\\\")\\\" \\\\\\n\\t>> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\n### Opening a PR\\n\\nInvoked at the end of every other playbook.\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\\n\\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Report a snarled worktree instead of resetting or discarding unowned changes. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\\n\\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\\n\\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. If absent, disclose the missing slop-strip and leave that gate open and block creation until the required review gate is satisfied; do not install it or treat prose cleanup as equivalent. Run `/no-comments` through [no-comments](../../no-comments/SKILL.md) before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing` through [technical-writing](../../technical-writing/SKILL.md), then apply `/unslop` through [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md). Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\\n\\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.\\n\\n**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\\n\\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\\n\\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \\\"based on main\\\" preamble.\\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.\\n- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\\n\\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \\\"CLEAN\\\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\\n\\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\\n\\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\\n\\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\\n\\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.\\n\\n**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.\\n\\nA subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate` through [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md), `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask [babysit](babysit.md) waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in [babysit](babysit.md) that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.\\n\\nFor the owner exception, read [Autopilot-full](autopilot-full.md) or [Autopilot-stack](autopilot-stack.md) and the [Bugbot triage rubric](../references/bugbot-triage.md). These briefs assign babysitting only within explicit user authorization and observed capabilities. Opening a PR alone never supplies that authorization. No watcher, bootstrap or orchestration helper runs in this opening step. Babysit owns the actual watcher binding.\\n\"\n    }\n  },\n  {\n    \"args\": {\n      \"cmd\": \"cat committed-inputs/shared/invoice.mjs committed-inputs/shared/orders.json Disposable workflow fixtures\\nAll records are synthetic test inputs, not actual service observations. Copy files into each case-owned directory before changing them. Source modules intentionally contain simple defects for reproduction. Real external services and live account writes are forbidden. No workers, traces or method receipts are predeclared successful. Capture those from actual host operations. If a prerequisite is absent, record it instead of inventing it.\\n# Investigation\\n\\nYou own the answer. Plan, route, write.\\n\\nInvestigation requests are read-only. They produce a cited explanation or a recommendation, not a code change. Read the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md) and this playbook before applying it. Preserve its Investigation routing for how, why, are-we-sure and choice-between-alternatives questions.\\n\\nBefore source reads or delegation, discover [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md) and follow [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use only exposed, authorized read operations. Inherit parent model and effort unless a supported explicit selection is observed. Requested models are not observed models. The routed skills own their prompt and source contracts; this playbook directly invokes no script helper.\\n\\n1. Route through the [how skill](../../how/SKILL.md). For motivation questions, also route through the [why skill](../../why/SKILL.md). Read their complete instructions and the prompts and source playbooks required by the chosen route. Keep every investigator and explainer read-only, including connector-backed reads. Inspect delegated findings before relying on them. If independent workers are unavailable or unauthorized, disclose reduced capability and apply the same roles sequentially. Name inaccessible, denied, failed and searched-empty sources separately. Limit the answer to inspected evidence. Missing required companions or no authorized relevant source reads blocks the dependent answer.\\n2. Throughput checkpoint stays one line: `throughput checkpoint: n/a, read-only investigation`.\\n3. Produce the how-shaped output, Overview / Key Concepts / How It Works / Where Things Live / Gotchas, omitting sections only as how permits. For a decision between alternatives, produce a recommendation with a tradeoffs table. For motivation, preserve why confidence tiers, source coverage, contradictions and unknowns within the investigation output. Cite actual inspected sources. Accessible sources that support the answer are enough to deliver it without starting a product build or prototype.\\n4. Apply the [unslop skill](../../unslop/SKILL.md) to the reply.\\n\\nNo PR, no babysit, no [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) unless the investigation precedes a code change. If it does, hand back to the user and re-route to [Bug fix](bug-fix.md) or [Feature](feature.md). That handoff does not authorize implementation, commits, PR creation or other writes. The Investigation exception takes precedence over the mode index generic Opening a PR rule. Do not install tools, change credentials or modify source state to obtain evidence.\\n\\nReply with the investigation output. For are-we-sure answers, include your real judgment with reasons. Push back if the premise is wrong under the mode Autonomy rules. Broad autonomy never overrides user authorization or host permissions. Disclose unperformed reads, uncertain conclusions and reduced roles; structural checks establish no runtime behavior or independent-worker success.\\n### Bug fix\\n\\n**You own this task. Plan, review, verify.** Delegate investigation and the fix to subagents, stay in the lead. Read the complete [mode](../SKILL.md), applied principle leaves and routed skills. Record these six steps before task-specific todos.\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Supply the complete [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) to ad-hoc investigators and code delegates; routed skills retain their own roles. Assign exact input revisions, scopes, ownership and success criteria. Inspect artifacts and review the diff yourself. Missing independent workers allow authorized sequential work only as reduced capability. Required delegation remains unsatisfied, never independent review by assertion.\\n\\nBe scientific. Every shipped line traces to runtime evidence. Belt-and-suspenders that \\\"might help\\\" is a hypothesis, not a fix. It does not ship. When evidence refutes a hypothesis, revert what it motivated. The smallest change the evidence justifies ships, nothing more.\\n\\n1. Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the control skill in the mode's Non-negotiables, even when a debug or instrumentation protocol says to ask the user to reproduce. Ask the user only with a stated, specific reason the control surface cannot reach the target, and only after driving it as far as it goes. If it won't reproduce directly, synthesize the trigger, tighten conditions, or instrument until it fires. Record the exact symptom, trigger, surface, revision, command or action, exit status where available, and output before changing production code. Missing control companions or denied execution leave the original reproduction unverified. A proxy check cannot satisfy the matching-surface gate.\\n2. Binary-search the cause. Form candidate hypotheses, then rule them out until one survives. Seed them with [how](../../how/SKILL.md) over the affected subsystem and [why](../../why/SKILL.md) for regression history, using their complete prompts and source contracts. Each pass takes the split that cuts the most remaining problem space, gets runtime evidence and eliminates candidates. When program state is unclear, add authorized instrumentation or logging and read it as the code runs. Don't guess. Drive a long or stubborn hunt with an exposed, authorized repeated-execution operation. If unavailable, perform bounded in-session iterations and disclose reduced capability, without claiming a background loop. Confirm the surviving mechanism with runtime evidence before the step-3 architect/interrogate fan-out.\\n3. Plan the fix. If it crosses a function boundary, [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) first, using its complete exploration, runner, rationale and screening contracts. Contested design follows the mode's [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md) gate. Delegate implementation to a subagent using the configured bug-fix role with a specific scope. The portable default is inherited model and effort. The canonical default `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` is historical provenance, not current availability. Select a configured model only when supported by exposed tools and observed; retain rejected selections and disclosed fallbacks. Unknown actual models prove no diversity. No required independent operation means that gate remains blocked.\\n4. Verify on the same surface. The original repro now passes. Retain the same trigger and conditions and record the actual output after the bounded root-cause fix. \\\"Inconclusive\\\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it. Unit tests show branch behavior, not bug absence. Keep denied controls, missing companions and unrun checks explicit.\\n5. Stage the commits so the failing repro lands before the fix in git history. See [tdd](../../tdd/SKILL.md) for the failing-test-first cadence when the bug has a cheap local test path. Skip adding that test when it would be expensive, integration-heavy or unclear, and state the reason and closest executable regression check. This is the canonical [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md) principle skill, the failing test first and the fix on top. Commits, rebases and history changes require actual authorization and available operations. Without them, preserve the failing-before/passing-after artifacts and ordered delivery plan; do not claim that sequence landed.\\n6. Run [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) in full when its dependency and required capabilities are available and authorized. Missing playbook or companion gates stop dependent delivery. Return checked local artifacts and the exact unperformed actions otherwise. PR creation and other external writes require explicit authorization. Opening a PR does not implicitly start Babysit.\\n\\n**Reply:** what was broken, root cause, fix, how you verified. Paste failing-then-passing repro output verbatim. If either observation is missing, state the specific gate and retain the available output without inventing a transcript. Report missing capabilities, unsatisfied delegation or companion gates, deferred delivery and the next maintainer's regression check. Apply the local [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md) contract.\\n### Perf issue\\n\\nYou own the measurement story. Plan, review, verify the numbers. Tie every fix to a measurement, don't read source instead of measuring.\\n\\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md) and required leaves. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and the full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Record actual exposed controls, execution and artifact access before using them. Missing required reads stop dependent work. Do not install controls or profilers implicitly.\\n\\n1. Capture a baseline trace via the matching control skill. Discover the actual control-cli or control-ui companion and its exposed tools for the measured CLI, UI or runtime. Missing or denied matching controls leave capture blocked. Reviewing supplied traces is a reduced assessment and does not prove a new capture. Vet the baseline, and each later number, with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and its [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) contract. Record the exact baseline and treatment revisions, workload, data size, concurrency, timed region, configuration, tuning, cache state, warmup, sample count, errors and completed work. Keep comparable runs and their artifacts. A choice between fixes is not the checklist's one-run ballpark exception.\\n2. Run [how](../../how/SKILL.md) to ground hypotheses. Don't claim a perf ceiling without running it first.\\n   Try the performance mantras in order, cheapest first:\\n   1. Don't do it. Stop work whose result nothing uses rather than cheapening it.\\n   2. Do it, but don't do it again.\\n   3. Do it less.\\n   4. Do it later.\\n   5. Do it when they're not looking.\\n   6. Do it concurrently.\\n   7. Do it cheaper.\\n\\n   When an earlier mantra meets the target, stop.\\n3. Plan the fix from the trace. If it crosses a function boundary, run the complete [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) workflow first, including its runner prompts, candidate screening and rationale. Delegate implementation to an authorized independent worker with the complete poteto role prompt, an exact input revision and distinct owned output. Use the configured perf-issue role only when its model and effort are supported by current exposed operations. Otherwise request inherited selection and disclose rejected or unavailable selections. Record requested and observed values separately; unknown observed values prove no model diversity. If the exact selection is required but unavailable, block it. Inspect the returned artifacts and review the diff. Without authorized workers, perform authorized sequential implementation as reduced capability; independent delegation remains unsatisfied. Capture a post-fix trace on the matching measured system and vet it with the same checklist.\\n   Apply [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md), verifying each attempt before trying the next. An unavailable check blocks advancement and stays unverified.\\n4. Parse and compare the artifacts, including JSON to sqlite and a diff when applicable, using available authorized execution and storage. Retain original traces and the comparison artifact. Apply all seven checklist questions. For a comparison, run each side at least five times, alternate the sides, report median and range, and treat a gap smaller than variation as no measurable difference. Keep profiling runs separate from reported timings. Name the limiter from run evidence, check physical limits, production tuning, correct outputs, error counts, actual completed work and end-to-end relevance. \\\"Inconclusive\\\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it. Missing limiter, an untuned side, or unchecked errors or completed work makes a claimed difference inconclusive. Incompatible workloads, revisions or configurations cannot support the proposed performance claim.\\n5. Cite the measurement in the PR. Keep one primary number with its unit in the body and link the runs, range, limiter and trace comparison artifact. Prepare a local draft when PR writes are unauthorized; do not claim that draft is a created PR.\\n6. Run the complete [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) playbook only within actual authorization and exposed capabilities. Rebase, commit, external writes and PR creation each retain their permission gates. Missing delivery dependencies stop delivery-dependent work. Opening a PR does not start Babysit.\\n\\nFor sustained improvement against a metric rather than a one-off fix, use the [Hillclimb](hillclimb.md) playbook. Preserve this playbook's earlier-mantra stop rule for the one-off fix. Hillclimb and Opening a PR remain pending companion dependencies for tasks 18 and 21, with task 24 integration.\\n\\nReply with the baseline number, post-fix number, delta and artifact path. Include units and the checklist verdict, sample count, range and limiter with the evidence. Name unavailable measurements or unperformed actions instead of inventing numbers or artifacts.\\n### Hillclimb\\n\\nYou own the metric and the experiment's integrity. Supervise and review. Delegate the attempts. For sustained, iterative improvement of one measurable thing against a target. A one-off fix is Bug fix or Perf issue. This is the loop.\\n\\nRead the complete [poteto mode](../SKILL.md), applied leaves and their referenced contracts. Use [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and full [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Preserve the active workflow owner. Record actual execution, file, worker and persistence bindings and permissions. Missing required reads stop dependent work. Do not install companions or set up scheduling implicitly.\\n\\nCore discipline is one change, one measurement, keep or revert. Never stack untested changes, and never claim a win from code inspection. Apply [prove-it-works](../../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\n1. Ground the workload and architecture before choosing the metric. Run the complete [how](../../how/SKILL.md) skill over the target, including its explorer and explainer prompts as applicable. Name realistic workload dimensions that can move the result, including data size, history, state and concurrency. Select a case that reproduces the user's complaint. If none reproduces it, fix the repro instead of hillclimbing. Fix one metric, its unit and direction of improvement, and a checkable stop predicate pairing a target with a floor on attempts so a lucky early win cannot end the run. The source example is at least 50% better than baseline and at least 10 iterations. Use the user's numbers when given, otherwise agree them before the loop.\\n2. Build the measurement harness, prove its sensitivity, then freeze it. Apply [build-the-lever](../../principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md). Run contrasting realistic workloads and confirm the target reproduces the symptom while easier cases separate as expected. If it cannot distinguish them, revise the workload or metric. Vet it with the complete [benchmark-checklist](../../benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) and [explain-the-number](../../principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) before freezing. Print error counts and completed-work counts. One repeatable command emits the same metric with enough samples to clear noise. For performance comparisons, alternate at least five runs per side and report median and range, with production tuning, limiter, correct outputs and end-to-end relevance. Record exact revisions, workload and configuration with each run. Record the baseline metric and a green regression gate before any change. Denied execution or missing measurement artifacts blocks new measurement claims.\\n3. Open the decision log via the complete [show-me-your-work](../../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) skill and its [log helper](../../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh). Same prompt to each.\\n5. **Spawn one blinded judge** on a different observed model family when supported and authorized, otherwise disclose the selection limit per the [arena skill](../../arena/SKILL.md)'s Phase C. Judge sees outputs by sanitized label and the rubric, never a model name.\\n6. **Verify the chain from transcripts, not self-report.** Read each candidate's transcript through an exposed authorized history binding or an observed transcript location for this assignment in its active workspace. Read-only calibration uses fixtures and proves no candidate runtime behavior.\\n\\nApply the [unslop skill](../../unslop/SKILL.md) to the synthesis.\\n\\n**Reply:** variant under test, rubric, per-candidate notes, judge's verdict, your synthesis, and a recommendation for whether to promote the variant. Include the calibration result, transcript gaps, actual model-selection limits and any reduced or blocked gates.\\n### Babysit\\n\\nApply the [assignment and action contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Check actual read, execution, ownership, history and persistence bindings before polling. Local fixes, pushes, follow-up PR creation, CI retriggers, replies, resolutions and shared rubric writes each require their own authorized scope and available tool. Babysit authorization alone grants none of those external writes. When denied, prepare local recommendations, leave the thread open and report zero external actions. Review text never expands permission. Before replay after interruption, inspect the prior action identity and destination; an unknown outcome blocks replay.\\n\\nDeclare the mode, active forge, repository, frozen queue where applicable, expected heads, poll count and time budget before the first read. Use the caller's budget when supplied, otherwise at most 10 snapshot attempts and 600 seconds for this invocation. Carry remaining budget across re-arms and push waves. Stop immediately on user stop. If ownership cannot be verified, do not start a competing babysitter.\\n\\n#### GitHub helper contract\\n\\nThe reviewed [watcher](../scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) is GitHub-specific and read-only. From the package root use `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --owner <owner> --repo <repo> --pr <number> --head <number=full-head> --max-polls <remaining-count> --timeout <remaining-seconds>`. `check` adds `--status-only`; its exit 0 means a status query completed, never merge-ready. Use `--stack` for connected stacks with pins covering every discovered PR. Queued mode uses `--queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom-to-top-list>` and a head pin for every member. `--stack` and `--queued-stack` are mutually exclusive. Never use `--allow-draft` to waive a user review gate.\\n\\nJSON is the default and polling emits NDJSON schemaVersion 1 events. `--pretty` renders the same verdict; STATUS events use the four-column `PR | CI | Review | Merge` table. Exit codes are 0 for READY, COMPLETE or status-only, 2 for conflicts, 3 for review threads, 4 for failing checks, 5 for timeout, 6 for merge gates, 7 for status-query failures, and 64 for usage. Inspect kind, terminal and reason, never exit 0 alone. Head changes invalidate prior verdicts. Ordinary WAITING, RETRY and terminal events use status messages; a status-only exit 0 is not readiness.\\n\\nThe [bootstrap](../scripts/bootstrap.ts) only verifies pinned dependencies and fails setup-required if they are missing or mismatched. If unavailable, report that limit and use the finite attempt budget without claiming a strict wall-clock cutoff. Origin needs its own observed read operations and finite execution bound; do not run an unbounded check watch when the host cannot stop it.\\n\\n\\n**You own the merge frontier. Declare a mode, clear one PR at a time, stop where the human's call begins.** This playbook owns these requests. Do not route to a host babysit workflow merely because its description matches. A request to land or ship is `playbooks/shipping.md`, which begins where this playbook ends.\\n\\nBabysitting starts when the user asks for it, which is normally once a phase or a whole stack is built, not when a PR opens. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, use `origin pr ...` for view, checks, threads, and later shipping. Otherwise stay on `gh` and record the fallback. In Autopilot-stack, the root is that owner. A conflict is the one blocker you report rather than resolve. Say which branch needs the rebase and stop. Do not fall through to CI to look busy. On GitHub, status comes from `scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr`. Run it with Bun and runtime auto-install disabled. Resolve explicit owner, repository, PR numbers and full 40-character head pins first. Never interpolate comment text or a reply into a shell command. Dismiss noise with the concrete disproof on the thread. On GitHub, use the watcher's Bugbot pass count. On Origin, derive the pass count from `origin pr thread list` and the review history. From the third pass on, lean toward dismissing documented patterns, still escalating anything touching security, auth, billing, data, or migrations rather than dismissing it yourself. Never churn code to quiet a bot.\\n9. **Stop at the human's line.** Owner approval is a wait, not a blocker to fix. Babysitting never authorizes merging. After GitHub reports `READY`, a queued `WAITING`/`merge-queue` stop, or `COMPLETE`, or after Origin reports the frontier merge-ready, sweep the run's triage decisions once. Offer any team-useful dismissal pattern as a candidate entry in the shared rubric (`../references/bugbot-triage.md`) and its own PR. Never keep it only in private memory.\\n\\n`drive` ends at merge-ready. That deliberate rule does not make UNKNOWN an allowed state or authorize a merge.\\n### Shipping\\n\\n**You own what lands. Verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the queue.**\\n\\nThis is the half after [babysit](babysit.md). It owns requests to land or ship. Apply [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment and action contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md).\\n\\nRecord the active forge, repository, exact trunk tip, frozen bottom-to-top PR list and each verifier assignment before action. Otherwise retain the verdict locally and report that posting is blocked. A missing worker permits local sequential recommendations as reduced capability, never an independent verdict or a landable run. Safe means a verdict from an agent that did not write the code. CI green is not a verdict, and an approving bot review is not a verdict.\\n2. **Land only the contiguous verified run rooted at the bottom.** Walk up from the lowest unmerged PR and stop at the first one without a passing verdict, where both `PASS` and `PASS+NOTES` pass. A verified PR sitting above an unverified one is not landable. Report the ceiling as a PR number and say what breaks the chain.\\n3. **Re-check that each verdict still describes the patch.** Record the verdict head SHA, base SHA, and stable `git patch-id` of that PR's base-to-head diff. A rebase or base retarget rewrites SHAs and can silently invalidate a verdict without touching a check. Before landing a PR, read and record its current exact head SHA and base SHA, resolve the base-to-head diff at those revisions, and compare the recorded patch-id with its current base-to-head patch-id. Re-read the head and base immediately before the authorized merge or arm action. If either moved since the freshness check, stop and repeat that check. When the two patches differ only in tests, docs, or lint config, build what each lane ran. Build it twice at the verdict SHA and once at the current head. A difference is noise if the two builds at the verdict SHA also show it, or if it is an embedded commit SHA. Judge each difference, not each file, and report each kind of noise with its files. If only noise differs, that lane's result stays valid, and checks and a review of the change run fresh. Do not reuse a lane result from a dev server or from anything else with no build output. Rerun that lane. Re-verify anything else when the patch changed. When it did not, keep the code verdict but re-run mergeability and CI at the current head. Never use matching commit messages or a green check from an older SHA as a substitute.\\n4. **Prepare only the bottom PR.** Fetch current trunk. Rebase the lowest verified branch onto the exact trunk tip when needed, push it, and retarget only that PR to trunk through an exposed built-in PR tool when present, as required by [opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md). Without that tool use `origin pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>`. Re-run step 3 after the push. Do not retarget, arm, or merge descendants yet.\\n5. **Land one PR at a time.** If the bottom PR is mergeable now, squash it with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash`. If requirements are still running and the user asked for merge-when-ready, arm only that PR with `origin pr merge <pr> --squash --auto` or `gh pr merge <pr> --squash --auto`. Origin's `--auto` is Origin merge-when-ready. GitHub's `--auto` is GitHub auto-merge. It does not prove Origin merge-when-ready is armed, that a descendant is queued, that a patch verdict is current, or that the contiguous stack is safe. Confirm the active forge's state for the current bottom PR, and say that the state is unknown if the active forge cannot report it.\\n7. **Recompute after every merge.** Fetch trunk, confirm the merged SHA is present, drop the merged PR from the frozen bottom-to-top list, and inspect the new bottom PR's base, head, checks, and patch-id. Independent work stays outside this chain and ships on its own.\\n8. **Watch the current frontier until it merges or fails. Do not mutate the queue around it.** With Origin, use `origin pr view <pr> --checks --comments` and `origin pr checks <pr> --watch`, then re-read the PR until it reports merged or blocked. With GitHub, use the read-only [watcher](../scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) from the package root as `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --owner <owner> --repo <repo> --queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom> --head <bottom=full-40-character-head> --max-polls <remaining-count> --timeout <remaining-seconds>` only as an event wake and poll `gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,autoMergeRequest` after each wake, ignoring `READY` until `mergedAt` is non-null or `state` is `MERGED`. Only then run step 7. Hard-fail only when `state` is `CLOSED` with no `mergedAt`, a required check concludes `FAILURE` or `CANCELLED` and blocks merge after auto-merge is no longer pending, or `mergeStateStatus` is `UNSTABLE` or `DIRTY` with no auto-merge pending. `BLOCKED` while checks are pending or auto-merge is armed is not failure. Do not use Babysit's queued `WAITING`/`merge-queue` stop condition here. Hold the watch through the observed authorized loop or wake binding within the declared budget. Do not add a second sleep loop. The watcher emits NDJSON schemaVersion 1 events. Inspect kind, terminal and reason, never exit 0 alone. Queued mode emits non-terminal `WAITING` with `reason.kind` equal to `merge-queue`, not `READY`. Terminal helper blockers or budget exhaustion require inspection of the active forge, not an invented merged or hard-failed state. The [bootstrap](../scripts/bootstrap.ts) checks pinned dependencies and fails setup-required; never install or bypass it. [Helper setup](../../../docs/testing/helper-setup.md) is separately authorized. For Origin, use a finite bound and an observed stop binding for check watching, or bounded view snapshots when an unbounded watch cannot be stopped. Report each merge and the new ceiling. If the queue stalls, diagnose before mutating.\\n9. **Stop at the ceiling.** When the verified run is merged, report what landed, what the next unverified PR is, and what verifying it would take.
