Produce architectural explanations at the level of a senior engineer onboarding onto a subsystem, enough to build a working mental model, not so much that it reads like annotated source code.\\n\\nBefore dispatch, read [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Bind worker operations to tools actually exposed and authorized in this session. Request the inherited parent model and effort unless a supported explicit selection is observed. Retain rejections and disclose replacements; an unavailable required selection is blocked. Record requested and observed selections separately, using unknown for unobserved values.\\n\\nKeep explorers and explainers read-only. Worker assignments record their role, distinct angle, exact input revision, identity and inspected results under the assignment contract. Reading a prompt does not register a worker. If independent workers are unavailable or unauthorized, disclose reduced capability and perform the same exploration and explanation roles sequentially. Never claim parallel or independent exploration from sequential work. If source access is unavailable or denied, report the gap and limit the explanation to inspected evidence.\\n\\n## Step 1. Assess Complexity\\n\\nIf the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore. The user can redirect.\\n\\n- **Simple** (a single module, a small utility, a narrow question such as \\\"how does function X work\\\"): no explorers. One explainer explores and explains in a single pass. Go to Step 2b.\\n- **Complex** (a subsystem spanning multiple files or services, a cross-cutting feature, a full architectural overview): use parallel explorers when available, then hand off to the explainer. Go to Step 2a.\\n\\nWhen in doubt, take the simple path.\\n\\n## Step 2a. Explore (complex questions only)\\n\\nDecompose the question into 2 to 4 exploration angles, each a distinct slice of the subsystem. Dispatch all explorers together through an observed worker binding, with distinct assignments:\\n\\n- Role: how explorer\\n- Model and effort: follow the model-role contract\\n- Access: read-only\\n\\nEach explorer gets the prompt in `references/explorer-prompt.md` with its angle filled in. If workers are unavailable, explore those distinct angles sequentially and retain separate findings. Then go to Step 3.\\n\\n## Step 2b. Direct Explain (simple questions)\\n\\nAssign one explainer worker that explores and explains in one pass:\\n\\n- Role: how explainer\\n- Model and effort: follow the model-role contract\\n- Access: read-only\\n\\nBuild its prompt from `references/explainer-prompt.md` without the explorer-findings section. The explainer reads and traces the source itself. If workers are unavailable, apply this role sequentially. Go to Step 4.\\n\\n## Step 3. Synthesize (complex questions only)\\n\\nOnce all explorer results have been inspected, assign one explainer worker to synthesize their findings into one explanation:\\n\\n- Role: how explainer\\n- Model and effort: follow the model-role contract\\n- Access: read-only\\n\\nBuild its prompt from `references/explainer-prompt.md` with every explorer's findings filled in. In reduced capability, synthesize the sequential findings under the same read-only role.\\n\\n## Step 4. Present\\n\\nPresent the explainer's output to the user. Light edits for clarity or context from the conversation are fine. Do not substantially rewrite it.\\n\\n## Output Format\\n\\nThe explanation uses the sections defined in `references/explainer-prompt.md`, dropping any that do not apply: Overview, Key Concepts, How It Works, Where Things Live, Gotchas.\\n---\\nname: architect\\ndescription: \\\"Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Architect\\n\\nDesign before implementing. Sketch types, function signatures, class shapes, and module boundaries with `not implemented` bodies and pseudocode. Synthesize across multiple model perspectives, then fill in code against the chosen sketch. If implementation proves the sketch wrong, throw it out and redesign.\\n\\n## Start\\n\\nOpen a todolist with one entry per phase before starting. If no task-list tool is exposed, keep the same phase list in the response and disclose that limit.\\n\\n1. Ground\\n2. Sketch\\n3. Agree\\n4. Implement\\n5. Scrap\\n\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\n\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use only observed exposed tools within user authorization. Read and follow each required skill in full. If direct invocation is unavailable, disclose that limit and execute its complete workflow inline as reduced capability. A missing required skill remains blocked. Record worker identities, requested and observed selections, rejections, result artifacts and limits.\\n\\nIndependent exploration requires authorized workers with observed spawn and result inspection. Without workers, disclose reduced capability and produce at least two sequential, structurally distinct alternatives using the complete arena workflow and runner discipline. Sequential alternatives are not independent model perspectives. Unverified or identical observed models do not establish model diversity. Denied source reads block grounding; denied writes leave a read-only design and an explicit implementation block.\\n\\n## Phase A: Ground the problem\\n\\nBuild a real mental model of every system the new code touches. Run the **how** skill over the relevant subsystems.\\n\\nNaming a file isn't grounding. Produce the traced model `how` prescribes. If the design redefines ownership or layering, also run the **why** skill on the existing shape so the rationale becomes a constraint, not a guess.\\n\\nSkip Phase A only when the work is genuinely greenfield with no surrounding system to integrate.\\n\\n## Phase B: Sketch\\n\\nRun the **arena** skill with the design-sketch task and the Phase A grounding artifacts. Pass `references/runner-prompt.md` as each runner's prompt. Each candidate produces a design package shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`.\\n\\nTake runner preferences from an available user-supplied `architect runners` configuration, in place of arena runner preferences. When no architect runner preferences are supplied, request inherited selection per the model-role contract. Preserve the goal of distinct model perspectives when supported and verified; inheritance does not establish diversity. Resolve aliases and rejected entries through the complete **arena** Phase A rules and current model-role contract. Select explicit models only when the exposed operation supports them; otherwise disclose inherited selection and unverified diversity. If an exact selection is required but unavailable, block that selection instead of silently replacing it.\\n\\nDesign it twice. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.\\n\\nScreen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.\\n\\nCompare viable candidates on interface depth. Prefer the design that hides more complexity behind a smaller, simpler public surface. A rich interface can keep call chains short by concentrating capability instead of scattering it across layers.\\n\\nArena returns one synthesized design package. The synthesis decision populates the rationale's \\\"Synthesis decision\\\" section.\\n\\n## Phase C: Agree (opt-in)\\n\\nDefault: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design when implementation is already authorized. No additional human checkpoint. Design-only scope does not authorize implementation.\\n\\nOpt in to a checkpoint when the invoker explicitly asks: \\\"/architect with checkpoint,\\\" \\\"stop and show me before implementing,\\\" or similar. Then surface the synthesized design and pause for sign-off.\\n\\nWith explicit commit authorization, the synthesis can ship as its own commit either way, as the \\\"scaffold first\\\" mode of the **foundational-thinking** principle skill. Planned and scoped breakage during fill-in is fine, per the **outcome-oriented-execution** principle skill. For adversarial pressure on the design before implementing, run the **interrogate** skill on the synthesized sketch.\\n\\nIf the human pushes back on the shape (in a checkpoint or after the fact), treat that as Phase A evidence. Re-ground and re-run Phase B before writing more code.\\n\\n## Phase D: Implement against the sketch\\n\\nReplace `not implemented` bodies with code, pseudocode with logic. The synthesized sketch is the contract.\\n\\nDeviations from the sketch are signal worth surfacing, not friction to absorb silently. If a function needs a parameter the sketch didn't anticipate, ask whether the sketch was wrong, the requirement was missed, or the implementation is overreaching.\\n\\n## Phase E: Scrap when the architecture is wrong\\n\\nIf implementation keeps producing friction the sketch can't absorb, throw the sketch out. Don't bolt fixes onto a wrong design, per the **redesign-from-first-principles** and **fix-root-causes** principle skills.\\n\\nThe signal is a *pattern*, not single instances. Tells:\\n\\n- The same shape of workaround appearing repeatedly across unrelated code.\\n- Multiple unrelated edge cases that all need special-case branches.\\n- Types that need escape hatches (`any`, casts, optional fields always set in practice) to compile.\\n- The \\\"we need a lock\\\" reflex when the sketch said the state wasn't shared.\\n- Callers having to know the abstraction's internal rules to use it.\\n- Two or more independent Phase D deviations of the same shape across the implementation.\\n\\nUse judgment. A few edge cases don't condemn an architecture. Some problems are legitimately complex. Complexity in the data is not complexity in the design.\\n\\nWhen you scrap:\\n\\n1. Re-run the **how** skill over what's been built.\\n2. Redesign as if the new constraints had been day-one assumptions, per redesign-from-first-principles.\\n3. Subtract before adding, per the **subtract-before-you-add** principle skill. The new sketch should be smaller than the old one before it grows.\\n4. Return to Phase B and re-run arena.\\n\\n## Outputs\\n\\nThe caller's usage is written first and the type sketch derived from it. One file with new types and signatures for small changes. Module map plus type definitions for larger work. The rationale ships alongside, shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`, including the usage sketch and the synthesis decision.\\n\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to generated rationale and reports without changing facts or principle meanings.\\n---\\nname: arena\\ndescription: \\\"Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Arena\\n\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Use only exposed, authorized operations. Read each applied principle leaf in full before dependent work. Missing required reads block that work. Invocation aliases are guidance, not proof of registered host commands.\\n\\nIndependent candidates and a fresh independent judge require observed worker operations and inspected artifacts. If unavailable, produce authorized sequential alternatives and parent comparison only as reduced capability. Do not claim independence, background execution, model diversity or a full arena pass. If independence is required, leave that gate blocked.\\n\\nFan out N parallel attempts at the same task. Read every candidate end to end. Pick the strongest as the base. Graft the best ideas from the others into it. Verify the synthesized result.\\n\\n## Start\\n\\nOpen an exposed todo list with one entry per phase before launching anything. Without one, use an authorized local Markdown checklist and disclose the reduced binding.\\n\\n1. Frame\\n2. Fan out\\n3. Cross-judge\\n4. Pick\\n5. Graft\\n6. Verify\\n\\n## Phase A: Frame\\n\\nThe N candidates will receive the same prompt, so the prompt is the contract.\\n\\n1. State the artifact each candidate is producing.\\n2. Derive the rubric. State what success looks like for *this* task, then turn it into 3-6 concrete gradeable criteria. The rubric is the picker's tool in Phase D. Candidates only see the task.\\n3. Pick the runners. Use an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena runners` preference if available. Otherwise request two inherited workers, one per seat. The source defaults used two specific model families. Their source-host slugs are not portable availability evidence. Select an explicit model or effort only from current exposed documentation or observed enumeration under the model-role contract. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry means omit explicit model selection. On rejection, record it and disclose a supported same-family alternative when available, otherwise an authorized inherited alternative. If the exact model is required, block instead. Record requested and observed model and effort separately, using unknown when unobserved. More seats can cover multiple design directions. Same model N times is appropriate when work is generation-bound rather than judgment-sensitive. Unknown models leave diversity unverified.\\n4. Assign output paths. Each candidate writes to its own authorized location, a git worktree where supported, otherwise a distinct local candidate directory. Follow [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Confirm isolation and write permissions before dispatch. Record immutable assignment identity, input SHA, owner, role and evidence links under the assignment contract. Workers never integrate shared files. Worktree creation and persistence require observed authorized capabilities.\\n\\n## Phase B: Fan out\\n\\nDispatch all N independent candidates together through the exposed worker operation, using observed background execution when available. Give each the same task, shared grounding path, its isolated output path, and instructions to produce both the artifact and a short rationale. Withhold the rubric from candidates. Inspect terminal results and artifact paths before accepting completion; a wait notification alone is insufficient.\\n\\nEach rationale names the alternatives the candidate considered and what it rejected.\\n\\nIf a candidate fails to produce output, proceed with N-1 and note the dropout in the synthesis record. One survivor means incomplete competition, even if its artifact is useful. Zero survivors blocks synthesis. Never integrate partial or cancelled artifacts as completed candidates.\\n\\n## Phase C: Cross-judge\\n\\nAfter all Phase B candidates reach terminal state and their accepted artifacts are inspected, choose one model from an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena cross-judge pool` preference. Without that preference, use an inherited worker or a supported explicit selection under the model-role contract. The source pool named the same two families as the runners; it does not establish portable model availability. Prefer a different observed model family from the parent's when available. Disclose rejected choices and supported fallbacks, or block if the exact choice is required.\\n\\nSpawn one fresh readonly judge worker. It sees the rubric and completed candidates by path label, scores each criterion, and recommends a base with rationale. It runs in parallel with the parent's reading in Phase D when observed background execution permits it, never with candidates still writing. The judge has no candidate write ownership. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified. Unavailable fresh judging remains a reduced or blocked gate, never an invented independent verdict.\\n\\n## Phase D: Pick a base\\n\\nRead every candidate end to end before picking.\\n\\nScore each candidate against the rubric criterion by criterion, not on holistic feel. Compare against the cross-judge. Agreement on the base confirms the pick. Disagreement means one of you is biased or the rubric was ambiguous. Read both rationales before deciding.\\n\\nPick the base on which candidate a future maintainer can extend most easily without breaking invariants. Prefer the cleaner boundary or smaller API when two feel tied, per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md).\\n\\nRecord the pick and the reason in a short synthesis note alongside the base artifact, including the cross-judge's verdict.\\n\\n## Phase E: Graft\\n\\nWalk each losing candidate once more and identify what is worth porting into the base. The signal is usually one or two things per candidate, not most of it.\\n\\nFold each graft in by hand, per [redesign-from-first-principles](../principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md). Don't paste mechanically. The result has to remain coherent under one mental model.\\n\\nRecord what was grafted, from which candidate, and what was rejected and why.\\n\\nWhen N candidates converge on the same shape, that is a strong agreement signal. Note the convergence in the record and deliver the consensus shape within authorized scope. No graft is needed. When N candidates wildly diverge, Phase A was under-specified. Reframe and re-run rather than averaging the divergence.\\n\\n## Phase F: Verify\\n\\nThe synthesized artifact has to hold up under the same scrutiny as any other output, per [prove-it-works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\nIf verification surfaces a problem the arena did not catch, either Phase A was wrong (re-frame and re-run) or one candidate caught it and you missed the graft (go back to Phase E). Don't paper over.\\n\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to the synthesis prose. External publication, commits, messages and setup require their own authorization.\\n\\n## Outputs\\n\\nOne synthesized artifact. One short synthesis note alongside, naming the base, the grafts and their source candidates, the rejections, the dropouts if any, and the verification result.\\n---\\nname: unslop\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Unslop\\n\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\n\\n## Process\\n\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\n\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\n\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\n\\n### Content\\n\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\"highlighting...\\\", \\\"ensuring...\\\", \\\"reflecting...\\\", \\\"showcasing...\\\", \\\"fostering...\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\"Experts believe\\\", \\\"Industry reports suggest\\\", \\\"Some critics argue\\\". Name the source or delete.\\n\\n### Language\\n\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\"is\\\".** \\\"serves as\\\", \\\"stands as\\\", \\\"boasts\\\", \\\"features\\\". Just say \\\"is\\\" or \\\"has\\\".\\n9. **\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\"from X to Y\\\" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\n\\n### Style\\n\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\"If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\n\\n### Communication artifacts\\n\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\"I hope this helps!\\\", \\\"Let me know if...\\\", \\\"Of course!\\\", \\\"Certainly!\\\", \\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\" Remove.\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\"Great question! You're absolutely right!\\\" Respond directly.\\n\\n### Filler\\n\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\"In order to\\\" becomes \\\"To\\\". \\\"Due to the fact that\\\" becomes \\\"Because\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" gets deleted.\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\" becomes \\\"may\\\".\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\"The future looks bright.\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\n\\n### Jargon\\n\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\"API surface\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\"Substrate\\\" becomes \\\"base\\\". \\\"Wedge in\\\" becomes \\\"add\\\". \\\"Vector\\\" becomes \\\"way\\\" or \\\"method\\\". \\\"Gold-plating\\\" becomes \\\"more than the job needs\\\". \\\"Ratchet\\\" becomes the mechanism's real name or \\\"a limit that only tightens\\\". \\\"Evacuate\\\" becomes \\\"move out\\\". \\\"Endgame\\\" becomes \\\"the last phase\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\n\\n### Plain speech\\n\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\"the database stays close at hand\\\", \\\"SQL you can read\\\", \\\"types that follow your schema\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\", \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\" and name the actor: \\\"queries are validated\\\" becomes \\\"the compiler validates queries\\\", \\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\" becomes \\\"the loader parses the file\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\"runs quickly\\\" becomes \\\"is fast\\\" or the number. \\\"significantly improves\\\" becomes the measured delta. Structural validation does not prove runtime behavior.\\n---\\nname: principle-redesign-from-first-principles\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Redesign From First Principles\\n\\nWhen integrating a change, don't bolt it onto the existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been there from the start.\\n\\n- Read all affected files and understand the current design\\n- Ask: \\\"if we were writing this from scratch with this new requirement, what would we build?\\\"\\n- Propagate the change through every reference: types, docs, examples, rationale sections\\n- Think about the whole redesign, then deliver it incrementally\\n\\nThis is the method for preserving option value when integrating changes into an existing design.\\n\\n## Capability and permission boundaries\\n\\nUse the [session capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before reading source, editing files or running checks. Apply the redesign within the authorized task. Propagating references does not grant permission to change unrelated files or perform external actions.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, provide a concrete redesign and incremental sequence as reduced capability. State which edits and checks were not performed. If affected source or design context is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep any redesign provisional. Claim implementation or verification only after observing the authorized operation.\\n---\\nname: show-me-your-work\\ndescription: \\\"Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. Validate every argument before any write.\\nif [ -z \\\"$1\\\" ]; then\\n    printf 'error: an explicit owned output path is required\\\\n' >&2\\n    exit 1\\nfi\\nfor value in \\\"$@\\\"; do\\n    case \\\"$value\\\" in\\n        *$'\\\\t'*|*$'\\\\n'*|*$'\\\\r'*)\\n            printf 'error: tabs, newlines and carriage returns are not allowed\\\\n' >&2\\n            exit 1\\n            ;;\\n    esac\\ndone\\nlogfile=\\\"$1\\\"\\nshift\\n\\nlogdir=\\\"$(dirname \\\"$logfile\\\")\\\"\\nif [ -n \\\"$logdir\\\" ] && [ \\\"$logdir\\\" != \\\".\\\" ] && [ ! -d \\\"$logdir\\\" ]; then\\n\\tmkdir -p \\\"$logdir\\\"\\nfi\\n\\n# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log\\n# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.\\nif [ ! -s \\\"$logfile\\\" ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'ts\\\\tphase\\\\tdecision\\\\twhy\\\\tevidence\\\\tresult\\\\n' >> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\nfi\\n\\nts=\\\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\\\"\\n# Record separators were rejected above. Prefix any cell\\n# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)\\n# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in\\n# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,\\n# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer\\n# opens the file.\\nclean() {\\n\\tlocal v\\n\\tv=\\\"$1\\\"\\n\\tcase \\\"$v\\\" in\\n\\t\\t=*|+*|-*|@*) printf \\\"'%s\\\" \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\t\\t*) printf '%s' \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\tesac\\n}\\nprintf '%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\n' \\\\\\n\\t\\\"$ts\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$1\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$2\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$3\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$4\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$5\\\")\\\" \\\\\\n\\t>> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\n#!/usr/bin/env bun\\nimport fs from \\\"node:fs\\\";\\nimport process from \\\"node:process\\\";\\nimport path from \\\"node:path\\\";\\n\\nconst RULE =\\n\\t\\\"Tests alone are not sufficient verification. Full verification requires unit evidence, live evidence, and performance evidence or justified non-applicability.\\\";\\nconst SUB_BLOCKS = [\\n\\t\\\"Depends on.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Files.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Build.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"You see.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, unit.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, live.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Verify, perf.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Review gate.\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Merge.\\\",\\n];\\nconst PROGRAM_H3 = [\\\"Arm the program\\\", \\\"Spawn owners\\\", \\\"PR mechanics\\\", \\\"Verdict and merge\\\", \\\"Boot recipe\\\"];\\nconst PROGRAM_MARKERS = [\\\"baseline\\\", \\\"status message\\\"];\\nconst HOW_TO_READ_MARKERS = [\\n\\t\\\"One box is one unit of work\\\",\\n\\t\\\"names the evidence\\\",\\n\\t\\\"Check a box only when its evidence exists\\\",\\n\\t\\\"playbooks/\\\",\\n\\tRULE,\\n];\\nconst PERF_ITEMS = [\\\"Metric.\\\", \\\"Probe.\\\", \\\"Baseline.\\\", \\\"Rule.\\\"];\\nconst BOX = /^\\\\s*- \\\\[[ x]\\\\] (.*)$/;\\n\\nconst file = process.argv[2];\\nif (!file || process.argv.length !== 3) {\\n\\tconsole.error(\\\"Usage: bun --no-install check-plan.mjs <pstack-plan.md>\\\");\\n\\tprocess.exit(2);\\n}\\n\\nlet raw;\\ntry { raw = fs.readFileSync(file, \\\"utf8\\\").split(/\\\\r?\\\\n/); }\\ncatch (error) { console.error(`${file}: cannot read plan (${error.code})`); process.exit(2); }\\nconst problems = [];\\nconst fail = (line, message) => problems.push(`${file}:${line}: ${message}`);\\n\\nlet start = 0;\\nif (raw[0] === \\\"---\\\") {\\n\\tstart = raw.indexOf(\\\"---\\\", 1) + 1;\\n}\\n\\nconst lines = [];\\nlet fence = false;\\nfor (let i = start; i < raw.length; i++) {\\n\\tconst text = raw[i];\\n\\tconst n = i + 1;\\n\\tif (/^```/.test(text)) fence = !fence;\\n\\tlines.push({ n, text, code: fence });\\n\\tif (fence) continue;\\n\\tconst prose = text\\n\\t\\t.replace(/`[^`]*`/g, \\\"`\\\")\\n\\t\\t.replace(/!\\\\[[^\\\\]]*\\\\]\\\\([^)]*\\\\)/g, \\\"\\\")\\n\\t\\t.replace(/\\\\]\\\\([^)]*\\\\)/g, \\\"]\\\");\\n\\tif (/[\\\\u2013\\\\u2014]/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"long dash\\\");\\n\\tif (/[\\\\u2018\\\\u2019\\\\u201c\\\\u201d]/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"curly quote\\\");\\n\\tif (/: \\\\S/.test(prose)) fail(n, \\\"mid-sentence colon\\\");\\n}\\n\\nconst h2 = (l) => (!l.code && l.text.startsWith(\\\"## \\\") ? l.text.slice(3).trim() : null);\\nconst sections = [];\\nfor (const l of lines) {\\n\\tconst title = h2(l);\\n\\tif (title !== null) sections.push({ title, n: l.n, body: [] });\\n\\telse if (sections.length) sections.at(-1).body.push(l);\\n}\\nconst find = (title) => sections.find((s) => s.title === title);\\nconst bodyText = (s) => s.body.map((l) => l.text).join(\\\"\\\\n\\\");\\nconst boxes = (ls) => ls.filter((l) => !l.code && BOX.test(l.text)).map((l) => ({ n: l.n, text: l.text.match(BOX)[1] }));\\n// This is a pstack template validator. It never edits a plan or validates\\n// implementation plans owned by another workflow.\\nif (!find(\\\"How to read this\\\") || !find(\\\"Program checklist\\\")) {\\n\\tconsole.error(`${file}:1: not a pstack multi-phase plan; leave other workflow plans unchanged`);\\n\\tprocess.exit(1);\\n}\\nconst capabilities = find(\\\"Capabilities\\\");\\nconst capabilityText = capabilities ? bodyText(capabilities) : \\\"\\\";\\nconst declared = {};\\nfor (const name of [\\\"Independent workers\\\", \\\"Live control\\\", \\\"Scheduling\\\", \\\"Remote\\\", \\\"Model selection\\\"]) {\\n\\tconst line = capabilities?.body.find((l) => !l.code && l.text.startsWith(`${name} `));\\n\\tconst match = line?.text.match(/^(.*?) (available|unavailable)\\\\. Evidence `([^`<>]+)`\\\\./);\\n\\tif (!match) fail(line?.n ?? 1, `${name}: missing capability evidence and available/unavailable declaration`);\\n\\telse declared[name] = { available: match[2] === \\\"available\\\", text: line.text, n: line.n };\\n}\\nconst capacity = Number(declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.text.match(/Capacity (\\\\d+)\\\\./)?.[1] ?? 0);\\nif (declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.available && capacity < 1) fail(declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"].n, \\\"available independent workers require observed capacity\\\");\\nfor (const [name, pattern] of [[\\\"Scheduling\\\", /\\\\/loop\\\\s|scheduled audit/i], [\\\"Remote\\\", /cloud VM|remote creation/i], [\\\"Model selection\\\", /Ten lanes on `|explicit model|grok-4/i]]) {\\n\\tfor (const line of lines) if (!line.code && pattern.test(line.text) && !declared[name]?.available) fail(line.n, `${name} claim lacks available capability evidence`);\\n}\\n\\nconst h1 = lines.findIndex((l) => !l.code && l.text.startsWith(\\\"# \\\"));\\nif (h1 === -1) fail(1, \\\"no H1 title\\\");\\nconst howToRead = find(\\\"How to read this\\\");\\nif (!howToRead) fail(1, 'no \\\"## How to read this\\\" section');\\nif (h1 !== -1 && howToRead) {\\n\\tconst intro = lines.slice(h1 + 1).filter((l) => l.n < howToRead.n && l.text.trim() !== \\\"\\\");\\n\\tif (intro.length >= 10) fail(lines[h1].n, `intro is ${intro.length} lines, under ten required`);\\n\\tfor (const marker of HOW_TO_READ_MARKERS) {\\n\\t\\tif (!bodyText(howToRead).includes(marker)) fail(howToRead.n, `How to read this lacks \\\"${marker}\\\"`);\\n\\t}\\n}\\n\\nconst program = find(\\\"Program checklist\\\");\\nif (!program) fail(1, 'no \\\"## Program checklist\\\" section');\\nelse {\\n\\tconst h3s = program.body.filter((l) => !l.code && l.text.startsWith(\\\"### \\\")).map((l) => l.text.slice(4).trim());\\n\\tlet cursor = 0;\\n\\tfor (const name of PROGRAM_H3) {\\n\\t\\tconst at = h3s.findIndex((t, i) => i >= cursor && t.startsWith(name));\\n\\t\\tif (at === -1) fail(program.n, `Program checklist lacks \\\"### ${name}\\\" in order`);\\n\\t\\telse cursor = at + 1;\\n\\t}\\n\\tfor (const marker of PROGRAM_MARKERS) {\\n\\t\\tif (!bodyText(program).includes(marker)) fail(program.n, `Program checklist lacks \\\"${marker}\\\"`);\\n\\t}\\n}\\n\\nconst close = find(\\\"Close the program\\\");\\nif (!close) fail(1, 'no \\\"## Close the program\\\" section');\\nconst programIndex = sections.indexOf(program);\\nconst closeIndex = sections.indexOf(close);\\nconst prSections = programIndex === -1 || closeIndex === -1 ? [] : sections.slice(programIndex + 1, closeIndex);\\nif (prSections.length === 0) fail(1, \\\"no PR sections between Program checklist and Close the program\\\");\\n\\nconst report = [];\\nfor (const pr of prSections) {\\n\\tconst heads = [];\\n\\tfor (const l of pr.body) {\\n\\t\\tif (l.code) continue;\\n\\t\\tconst m = l.text.match(/^\\\\*\\\\*([^*]+)\\\\*\\\\*(.*)$/);\\n\\t\\tif (m && SUB_BLOCKS.includes(m[1])) heads.push({ name: m[1], n: l.n, rest: m[2].trim(), lines: [] });\\n\\t\\telse if (heads.length) heads.at(-1).lines.push(l);\\n\\t}\\n\\tconst names = heads.map((h) => h.name);\\n\\tif (names.join(\\\"|\\\") !== SUB_BLOCKS.join(\\\"|\\\")) {\\n\\t\\tfail(pr.n, `${pr.title}: sub-blocks are [${names.join(\\\", \\\")}], expected [${SUB_BLOCKS.join(\\\", \\\")}]`);\\n\\t}\\n\\tconst block = (name) => heads.find((h) => h.name === name);\\n\\tconst counts = {};\\n\\tfor (const h of heads) counts[h.name] = boxes(h.lines).length;\\n\\n\\tconst depends = block(\\\"Depends on.\\\");\\n\\tif (depends && depends.rest === \\\"\\\") fail(depends.n, `${pr.title}: Depends on names nothing`);\\n\\tfor (const name of [\\\"Files.\\\", \\\"Build.\\\", \\\"You see.\\\", \\\"Verify, unit.\\\", \\\"Merge.\\\"]) {\\n\\t\\tconst b = block(name);\\n\\t\\tif (b && boxes(b.lines).length === 0) fail(b.n, `${pr.title}: ${name} has no box`);\\n\\t}\\n\\tfor (const name of [\\\"Verify, unit.\\\", \\\"Verify, live.\\\", \\\"Verify, perf.\\\"]) {\\n\\t\\tconst b = block(name);\\n\\t\\tif (b && !b.rest.startsWith(RULE)) fail(b.n, `${pr.title}: ${name} does not open with the rule`);\\n\\t}\\n\\n\\tconst live = block(\\\"Verify, live.\\\");\\n\\tif (live) {\\n\\t\\tconst status = live.rest.match(/Status (full|reduced|blocked)\\\\./)?.[1];\\n\\t\\tconst laneCount = Number(live.rest.match(/Lanes (\\\\d+)\\\\./)?.[1] ?? -1);\\n\\t\\tif (!status) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: live requires Status full, reduced, or blocked`);\\n\\t\\tif (status === \\\"full\\\" && (!declared[\\\"Live control\\\"]?.available || !declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.available)) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: full live verification requires control and independent workers`);\\n\\t\\tif (status === \\\"full\\\" && laneCount > capacity) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: live lane count exceeds observed worker capacity`);\\n\\t\\tif ((status === \\\"reduced\\\" || status === \\\"blocked\\\") && !/Reason .+\\\\. Evidence `[^`<>]+`\\\\./.test(live.rest)) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: reduced or blocked live requires reason and evidence`);\\n\\t\\tif ((status === \\\"reduced\\\" || status === \\\"blocked\\\") && /full success|fully verified|every lane.*PASS/i.test(bodyText(pr))) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: reduced or blocked live cannot claim full success`);\\n\\t\\tconst lanes = boxes(live.lines).map((b) => ({ ...b, m: b.text.match(/^Lane (\\\\d+)\\\\. /) }));\\n\\t\\tconst numbers = lanes.filter((b) => b.m).map((b) => Number(b.m[1]));\\n\\t\\tif (!Number.isInteger(laneCount) || laneCount < 0 || laneCount > 100 || numbers.length !== laneCount || numbers.some((n, i) => n !== i + 1) || (status !== \\\"blocked\\\" && laneCount === 0)) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: lanes must be ordered 1 through declared count`);\\n\\t\\tfor (const lane of lanes) {\\n\\t\\t\\tif (!lane.m) fail(lane.n, `${pr.title}: live box is not a lane`);\\n\\t\\t\\telse if (!/Save `[^`<>]+`/.test(lane.text)) fail(lane.n, `${pr.title}: lane ${lane.m[1]} names no evidence artifact`);\\n\\t\\t\\telse if (!lane.text.includes(\\\"Pass when\\\")) fail(lane.n, `${pr.title}: lane ${lane.m[1]} has no pass predicate`);\\n\\t\\t\\tconst original = live.lines.find((l) => l.n === lane.n)?.text ?? \\\"\\\";\\n\\t\\t\\tif (/^\\\\s*- \\\\[x\\\\]/.test(original)) {\\n\\t\\t\\t\\tconst receipt = lane.text.match(/Observed head `([a-f0-9]{40})`\\\\. Evidence `([^`<>]+)`\\\\./);\\n\\t\\t\\t\\tif (!receipt) fail(lane.n, `${pr.title}: checked live requires observed head and evidence receipt, a checkbox is not proof`);\\n\\t\\t\\t\\telse {\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tconst artifact = path.resolve(path.dirname(path.resolve(file)), receipt[2]);\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\ttry { if (!fs.statSync(artifact).isFile() || fs.statSync(artifact).size === 0) throw new Error(\\\"empty\\\"); }\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tcatch { fail(lane.n, `${pr.title}: checked live evidence receipt is missing or empty`); }\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\tif (status === \\\"blocked\\\" && live.lines.some((l) => /^\\\\s*- \\\\[x\\\\]/.test(l.text))) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: blocked live cannot have checked success boxes`);\\n\\t\\tif (laneCount > 0 && !/Regression.*trunk.*head/i.test(lanes[0]?.text ?? \\\"\\\")) fail(live.n, `${pr.title}: first lane must name regression against trunk and head`);\\n\\t}\\n\\n\\tconst perf = block(\\\"Verify, perf.\\\");\\n\\tif (perf) {\\n\\t\\tconst text = perf.lines.map((l) => l.text).join(\\\"\\\\n\\\");\\n\\t\\tconst items = boxes(perf.lines).map((b) => b.text.split(\\\" \\\")[0]);\\n\\t\\tif (/Not applicable\\\\./.test(text)) {\\n\\t\\t\\tif (!/Not applicable\\\\. Reason .+\\\\. Evidence `[^`<>]+`\\\\./.test(text) || items.length) fail(perf.n, `${pr.title}: performance non-applicability needs separate reason and evidence, without success boxes`);\\n\\t\\t} else if (items.join(\\\"|\\\") !== PERF_ITEMS.join(\\\"|\\\")) fail(perf.n, `${pr.title}: perf boxes are [${items.join(\\\", \\\")}], expected [${PERF_ITEMS.join(\\\", \\\")}]`);\\n\\t}\\n\\n\\tconst gate = block(\\\"Review gate.\\\");\\n\\tif (gate) {\\n\\t\\tconst gateBoxes = boxes(gate.lines);\\n\\t\\tconst applicable = /(?:^|\\\\. )Interaction applicable\\\\./.test(gate.rest);\\n\\t\\tconst notApplicable = /(?:^|\\\\. )Interaction not applicable\\\\. Reason .+\\\\. Evidence `[^`<>]+`\\\\./.test(gate.rest);\\n\\t\\tif (applicable === notApplicable) fail(gate.n, `${pr.title}: explicit interaction applicability required, with reason and evidence for non-applicability`);\\n\\t\\tif (!declared[\\\"Independent workers\\\"]?.available && !/Reduced review\\\\. Reason .+\\\\. Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Show me your work\\n\\nKeep one canonical log.\\n\\n## The format\\n\\nA single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.\\n\\nCopy [references/decision-log-template.tsv](references/decision-log-template.tsv) (the header row) to start a clean log. Columns:\\n\\n- **ts.** ISO8601 timestamp.\\n- **phase.** The phase or workstream.\\n- **decision.** What was chosen or done, one line.\\n- **why.** The reason in plain words. If a principle drove it, say it plainly, not as a jargon tag.\\n- **evidence.** A link or path that proves it: commit SHA, PR number, `file:line`, or an artifact, trace, or screenshot path. Never a paragraph.\\n- **result.** The outcome or predicate state: `tests green`, `reverted`, `pixel-diff 0`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `open`.\\n\\nAn example, plain-spoken so a reviewer reads it at a glance.\\n\\n```\\nts\\tphase\\tdecision\\twhy\\tevidence\\tresult\\n2026-05-24T09:02:00Z\\tframe\\tcounted the work first, about 100 components and roughly 75 hours\\twanted to know the size before starting a long run\\tcommit 3a9f1c2\\tfound 5 things to sort out before starting\\n2026-05-24T09:40:00Z\\tharness\\ttook screenshots of the old version before changing anything\\tso we can compare old against new and catch any visual change\\tscripts/snapshot.sh, baseline/\\tsaved 120 reference screenshots\\n2026-05-24T11:15:00Z\\twidget\\tmoved the widget styles over without changing how it looks\\tkeep the change small and the result identical\\tcommit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0\\tlooks identical, tests pass\\n2026-05-24T12:30:00Z\\twidget\\tthrew out a helper's work because its screenshots were blank\\tchecked the real files instead of trusting its summary\\tworktree reset\\treverted, tightened the instructions for next time\\n```\\n\\n## Logging a row\\n\\nWrite each entry the way you'd tell a teammate what you did. Plain words, concrete actions, no AI speak or abstract jargon (the **unslop** skill applies to log text too).\\n\\nUse the helper [scripts/log.sh](scripts/log.sh) with `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>` through an authorized execution binding. Pass an explicit nonempty local output path that this task owns. The helper rejects tabs, newlines and carriage returns in any argument before creating directories or writing bytes. It stamps `ts`, writes the header on first use, preserves previous rows, and prefixes any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` with a single quote. Use this helper for generated or user-supplied cells so validation and formula protection apply consistently. Host execution still requires an authorized binding.\\n\\nLog decision points and checkpoints, not every action: a fork chosen, a unit completed with its verification result, a pivot or revert with its trigger, a blocker surfaced, a gate fixed. For loop runs, one row per iteration. Skip the trivial and self-evident.\\n\\nA run is one agent conversation, including its later turns and any summary of it. A pickup, a replacement agent, or a new chat starts a new run. When a run adds to a log that already has rows, its first row has phase `start`, and so does its first row after another run's `start` row. So a run that comes back to a log in a later turn first reads the log's last rows to see whether another run wrote since. A `start` row names the `ts` range of the rows before it that this run did not write, and its evidence names this run, such as its agent id. Use phase `start` for nothing else.\\n\\n## Where it lives\\n\\nBy default the log is a working artifact, not committed. Keep it at `decisions.tsv` in the work dir, or `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` when several efforts run at once, and leave it out of git.\\n\\nCommit it only when the work is ambitious enough that a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result.\\n\\n## Rules\\n\\n- Append-only. A wrong call gets a new row that supersedes it. Never edit or delete history.\\n- Prefer evidence produced by committed scripts over hand-made one-offs (the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill).\\n\\n## Audit the log against the transcript\\n\\nAt the end of the run, before handing back, check the log told the truth. Discover this run's transcript through the current session's history binding, or an explicitly identified transcript in the active workspace. The source used `agent-transcripts/`; do not assume the host provides that directory. Never search unrelated private chats or global transcript directories. If this run's transcript is inaccessible or incomplete, record the gap and do not claim a complete transcript audit. Walk this run's rows against what actually happened. Each stretch of them begins at one of this run's `start` rows, or at the first row if this run created the log, and ends at the next `start` row of another run:\\n\\n- Check that every row maps to a real decision or action.\\n- Check that each row's evidence resolves and shows what the row claims.\\n- A fork, pivot, or abandoned approach that shaped the work but isn't logged is a gap. Add it.\\n\\nCorrect the log, not the story. The audit never edits or removes a row, even an invented one. When a row records neither a real decision nor a real action, or its claim or evidence is wrong, add a row that supersedes it with what actually happened and a pointer that resolves. This audit does not check rows outside this run's stretches. If this run's own work shows one of them is wrong, supersede it like any wrong call.\\n\\n## Cross-model review of the trail\\n\\nBefore handing back, use an authorized exposed independent-worker binding to request a reviewer on a different model family from the one that did the work. Follow [model selection](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Observe the worker identity, result and actual model family before claiming independent cross-model review. If no authorized worker or verified different family is available, record that review as blocked. An authorized sequential scan is reduced capability and does not satisfy this review requirement. Self-review is not a substitute. The subagent reads the audit trail and the run's transcript, then flags what the user should pay attention to. Not a redo of the work, a scan for what's suboptimal or risky.\\n\\n- Decisions logged with weak or absent evidence.\\n- Verification steps skipped or claimed without proof in the transcript.\\n- Choices that look risky in hindsight (premature, scope-creeping, papering over a symptom).\\n- Gaps the user would otherwise miss on a casual skim.\\n\\nEvery reply for a run that produced a trail ends with an \\\"Attention\\\" section. Lead with the reviewer's model on its own line (`reviewed by <model>`), then list each flag pointing to specific rows or moments. \\\"No flags\\\" is a valid value. The model name is not.\\n\\n## Reviewing the trail\\n\\nRead top to bottom, follow the evidence pointers, spot-check. GitHub renders a committed TSV as a table. `column -s$'\\\\t' -t decisions.tsv` renders it in a terminal.\\n\\n## Composing this skill\\n\\nOther skills route their audit trail here instead of inventing one. Reference it by name and let it own the format. Don't restate the columns.\\n\\n## Host capabilities and safety\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for history, execution, persistence and reviewer bindings. Write only to an authorized local path, then read back the saved trail before claiming persistence. A log is evidence of recorded decisions, not proof of unattended execution or recovery. Do not include credentials, tokens, raw secret-bearing output or unrelated private data. Use a safe evidence pointer or a redacted local artifact instead. Record only observed results; unresolved predicates stay `open` or `INCONCLUSIVE`.\\n\\nThe default local trail does not authorize a commit. Commit, publish, message or other external action requires explicit authorization. Preserve append-only history and scope every transcript audit to this run. When review is blocked, keep the Attention section and state `reviewed by unknown` if no actual reviewer model was observed, followed by the capability gap. Never use `No flags` to imply an unperformed review.\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).\\n# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\nset -euo pipefail\\n\\nif [ \\\"$#\\\" -ne 6 ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\\\\n' >&2\\n\\texit 1\\nfi\\n\\n# The caller owns the output path. Validate every argument before any write.\\nif [ -z \\\"$1\\\" ]; then\\n    printf 'error: an explicit owned output path is required\\\\n' >&2\\n    exit 1\\nfi\\nfor value in \\\"$@\\\"; do\\n    case \\\"$value\\\" in\\n        *$'\\\\t'*|*$'\\\\n'*|*$'\\\\r'*)\\n            printf 'error: tabs, newlines and carriage returns are not allowed\\\\n' >&2\\n            exit 1\\n            ;;\\n    esac\\ndone\\nlogfile=\\\"$1\\\"\\nshift\\n\\nlogdir=\\\"$(dirname \\\"$logfile\\\")\\\"\\nif [ -n \\\"$logdir\\\" ] && [ \\\"$logdir\\\" != \\\".\\\" ] && [ ! -d \\\"$logdir\\\" ]; then\\n\\tmkdir -p \\\"$logdir\\\"\\nfi\\n\\n# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log\\n# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.\\nif [ ! -s \\\"$logfile\\\" ]; then\\n\\tprintf 'ts\\\\tphase\\\\tdecision\\\\twhy\\\\tevidence\\\\tresult\\\\n' >> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\nfi\\n\\nts=\\\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\\\"\\n# Record separators were rejected above. Prefix any cell\\n# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)\\n# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in\\n# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,\\n# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer\\n# opens the file.\\nclean() {\\n\\tlocal v\\n\\tv=\\\"$1\\\"\\n\\tcase \\\"$v\\\" in\\n\\t\\t=*|+*|-*|@*) printf \\\"'%s\\\" \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\t\\t*) printf '%s' \\\"$v\\\" ;;\\n\\tesac\\n}\\nprintf '%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\t%s\\\\n' \\\\\\n\\t\\\"$ts\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$1\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$2\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$3\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$4\\\")\\\" \\\"$(clean \\\"$5\\\")\\\" \\\\\\n\\t>> \\\"$logfile\\\"\\n### Opening a PR\\n\\nInvoked at the end of every other playbook.\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\\n\\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Report a snarled worktree instead of resetting or discarding unowned changes. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\\n\\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\\n\\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. If absent, disclose the missing slop-strip and leave that gate open and block creation until the required review gate is satisfied; do not install it or treat prose cleanup as equivalent. Run `/no-comments` through [no-comments](../../no-comments/SKILL.md) before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing` through [technical-writing](../../technical-writing/SKILL.md), then apply `/unslop` through [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md). Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\\n\\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.\\n\\n**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\\n\\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\\n\\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \\\"based on main\\\" preamble.\\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.\\n- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\\n\\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \\\"CLEAN\\\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\\n\\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\\n\\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\\n\\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\\n\\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`.
