      "path": "fixtures/cases/fresh-worker-mode/outputs/principle-bindings.verbatim.md",
      "bytes": 5360,
      "sha256": "207577b4cb4bd19d2b2e715bfdab65b313b37e99944275555369d977de1e277f",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-fresh-worker-mode",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "## Principles\n\nRead the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies.\n\n**Core**\n\n- **Laziness Protocol** (**principle-laziness-protocol**). Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\n- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.\n- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.\n- **Attack the Premise** (**principle-attack-the-premise**). Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.\n- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.\n- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.\n- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.\n- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.\n- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.\n- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.\n\n**Architecture**\n\n- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.\n- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.\n- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.\n- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.\n- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.\n- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or \"it compiles\".\n- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.\n- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.\n- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation** (**principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**). Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\n- **Explain the Number** (**principle-explain-the-number**). Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\n\n**Delegation**\n\n- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.\n- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask \"should I do X?\" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.\n\n**Meta**\n\n- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\n"
    },

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "### Feature\n\nYou own the design. Plan, review, verify. Delegate implementation. Stay in the lead.\n\nRead [poteto-mode](../SKILL.md) in full before work. Follow its Comments rules and required companion gates. Discover authorized operations through [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md). Use [assignment and integration](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md) and [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md). Keep the playbook steps verbatim in an exposed todo list, or an authorized local checklist with the reduced binding disclosed. Invocation aliases name workflows, not registered host commands.\n\n1. Run [how](../../how/SKILL.md) over the affected subsystem. Ground the intended user outcome in traced source and caller behavior.\n2. Run [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) for parallel design exploration. Follow its complete design and arena contracts. Preserve sequential alternatives only as reduced capability when independent workers are unavailable. Required independence remains blocked.\n3. Write the throughput checkpoint as four todo items. Keep any dimension that does not apply, such as a single file or no fan-out, with `n/a: <reason>` rather than dropping it.\n   - Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\n   - Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services, or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\n   - Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Serialize only for real invariants.\n   - Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\n4. Delegate code-writing to a fresh independent worker with the entire [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and exact file pointers. Use the configured feature role when supported and observed. Otherwise request inherited model and effort. Record requested and observed selections separately, with unknown for unobserved values. Assign exact file paths, a named data shape and its organizing structure, and success criteria tied to the user outcome. Choose the structure before the delegate writes logic under [model-the-domain](../../principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md). Prefer a state machine over scattered booleans, a table or registry over branching, or a typed model over repeated shape assumptions. When implementation admits multiple valid shapes, such as error handling, abstraction layer or test structure, delegate through [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Its runners surface alternatives and its fresh cross-judge guards the pick. This gate is mandatory. There is no skip-with-reason escape, and Laziness Protocol does not override it. The gain is review separation, not lines saved. A worker forbidden to spawn owns the diff directly and returns it to the lead for the same review separation. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \"standing by\". Without authorized independent workers, direct implementation can be an explicit reduced result, but it does not satisfy independent review separation. The lead reviews the actual diff and owns the summary. Apply the mode's Comments rules. Make surgical edits and re-ground upstream-derived files against their source. Port shared-primitive improvements to all consumers and verify each. Commit each verified unit when authorized and after the mode's commit gates.\n5. Verify on the matching surface using available authorized control tools and the mode's matching companion requirements. Tie observed evidence to the intended user outcome. \"Inconclusive\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it and retain the unverified gate. Compilation or structural checks do not prove the feature works.\n6. Rebase into small, ordered commits and stack follow-ups when authorized and safe for concurrent work. Use [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md). Build, verify and commit each small unit before the next. An unrun required check blocks advancement. If commit or rebase is unavailable or unauthorized, return the checked diff and ordered delivery plan with those operations unperformed.\n7. If the design is contested, run [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md) before shipping. Preserve its review rubric, independence and observed model-diversity limits. Sequential review does not become independent or multi-model review.\n8. Run the Opening a PR playbook at `opening-a-pr.md` in this directory. This caller requires that complete playbook, its review gates and actual PR result inspection. If the file is absent, report the exact deferred dependency and stop PR-dependent work. Do not reconstruct it from this paragraph. External PR creation and push require actual authorization. Return a local reviewable result when those actions are unavailable or unauthorized. Never claim a local draft is a created PR. Opening a PR does not start Babysit.\n\nCode-coupled work, such as one feature or one migration, goes to a single owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out internally after the blocking phase when authorized and supported. Parent-level fan-out is for slices that produce independent artifacts, such as audits, cross-subsystem investigations or competing experiments. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries. Spawn a fresh owner rather than chaining interrupts. Distinct owned paths and inspected results remain prerequisites for integration.\n\nReply with what you built, what you chose and why, the throughput checkpoint, and open decisions. Use tables for design alternatives. Name the end user's changed behavior and what the next maintainer inherits. Link observed verification artifacts and actual PRs. Disclose missing companions, unavailable workers, unobserved models, failed checks and deferred dependencies beside the affected claim. Keep incomplete gates visible.\n\n\nLocal checklist status\nSteps1-3 grounded. Step4 pending independent designs, judge and no-spawn implementation. Step5 local Bun API checks only; matching companion unavailable. Step6 commits/rebase skipped by explicit prohibition. Step7 skip unless design contested. Step8 external creation blocked by policy.\n"

      "text": "diff --git a/committed-inputs/shared/invoice.mjs b/outputs/implementation/working/invoice.mjs\nindex 411a960..151e3fc 100644\n--- a/committed-inputs/shared/invoice.mjs\n+++ b/outputs/implementation/working/invoice.mjs\n@@ -1,5 +1,14 @@\n export function calculate(rows){return rows.reduce((n,r)=>n+r.qty*r.unitPrice,0)}\n-export function adapter(invoice){return calculate(invoice.rows)}\n-export function facade(invoice){return adapter(invoice)}\n-export function controller(invoice){return {total:facade(invoice)}}\n+function readDiscount(value){\n+  if(value===undefined)return 0;\n+  if(typeof value!==\"number\"||!Number.isFinite(value)||value<0)throw new RangeError(\"invalid discount\");\n+  return value;\n+}\n+function invoiceTotal(invoice){\n+  const discount=readDiscount(invoice.discount);\n+  const subtotal=calculate(invoice.rows);\n+  return discount===0?subtotal:Math.max(0,subtotal-discount);\n+}\n+export {invoiceTotal as adapter,invoiceTotal as facade};\n+export function controller(invoice){return {total:invoiceTotal(invoice)}}\n export function format(n){if(!Number.isFinite(n))throw new Error(\"nonfinite\");return n.toFixed(2)}\n"

    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/fresh-worker-mode/outputs/implementation/working/invoice.mjs",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "export function calculate(rows){return rows.reduce((n,r)=>n+r.qty*r.unitPrice,0)}\nfunction readDiscount(value){\n  if(value===undefined)return 0;\n  if(typeof value!==\"number\"||!Number.isFinite(value)||value<0)throw new RangeError(\"invalid discount\");\n  return value;\n}\nfunction invoiceTotal(invoice){\n  const discount=readDiscount(invoice.discount);\n  const subtotal=calculate(invoice.rows);\n  return discount===0?subtotal:Math.max(0,subtotal-discount);\n}\nexport {invoiceTotal as adapter,invoiceTotal as facade};\nexport function controller(invoice){return {total:invoiceTotal(invoice)}}\nexport function format(n){if(!Number.isFinite(n))throw new Error(\"nonfinite\");return n.toFixed(2)}\n"

    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/fresh-worker-mode/outputs/implementation/invoice.test.mjs",
      "bytes": 1633,
      "sha256": "bac3deadc82ada2750c908f3191053929f1f26d11095f1a570ab90301cb57b04",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-fresh-worker-mode",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import {test,expect} from 'bun:test';\nimport {calculate,adapter,facade,controller,format} from './working/invoice.mjs';\nconst rows=Object.freeze([Object.freeze({qty:2,unitPrice:10}),Object.freeze({qty:1,unitPrice:10})]);\ntest('legacy subtotal and formatting',()=>{\n expect(calculate(rows)).toBe(30);\n expect(format(30)).toBe('30.00');\n expect(()=>format(Infinity)).toThrow('nonfinite');\n expect(calculate([{qty:'2',unitPrice:3}])).toBe(6);\n});\ntest('invoice totals and compatible named exports',()=>{\n expect(controller({rows})).toEqual({total:30});\n expect(controller({rows,discount:0})).toEqual({total:30});\n expect(controller({rows,discount:5})).toEqual({total:25});\n expect(controller({rows,discount:40})).toEqual({total:0});\n expect(adapter({rows,discount:5})).toBe(25);\n expect(facade({rows,discount:5})).toBe(25);\n});\ntest('invalid supplied discounts reject without coercion',()=>{\n for(const discount of [-1,NaN,Infinity,-Infinity,'5',null,{},true])expect(()=>controller({rows,discount})).toThrow(RangeError);\n expect(controller({rows,discount:5})).toEqual({total:25});\n});\ntest('zero discount preserves negative subtotal',()=>{\n const negative=[{qty:1,unitPrice:-5}];\n expect(controller({rows:negative})).toEqual({total:-5});\n expect(controller({rows:negative,discount:0})).toEqual({total:-5});\n expect(controller({rows:negative,discount:1})).toEqual({total:0});\n});\ntest('frozen input remains intact after total calculation',()=>{\n const invoice=Object.freeze({rows,discount:5});\n expect(controller(invoice)).toEqual({total:25});\n expect(invoice).toEqual({rows:[{qty:2,unitPrice:10},{qty:1,unitPrice:10}],discount:5});\n});\n"
    },

Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Model the Domain\\n\\nEncode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals.\\n\\n**Why:** Scattered booleans, repeated shape assumptions, and branching spread across files are accidental complexity. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap. Recovering it later reads as a refactor and gets deferred.\\n\\n**Reach for structures like these:**\\n\\n- A state machine instead of scattered booleans, phases, or lifecycle checks.\\n- A typed object/model instead of loose parameters or repeated shape assumptions.\\n- A map, registry, lookup table, or discriminated union instead of branching spread across files.\\n- A reducer or command/event model instead of ad hoc state mutations.\\n- A module organized around one body of domain knowledge instead of a sequence such as load, validate, transform, and save. Execution order is not ownership.\\n- A small module boundary that gathers repeated behavior, ownership, or invariants.\\n- A queue, cache, index, graph/tree, or normalized collection where the data access pattern calls for it.\\n- Any other structure that fits. When none fits, work out what the code must never allow and how the data gets read, then find the structure that encodes exactly that.\\n\\nDo not force an abstraction. Prefer boring code if the current shape is already clear, local, and unlikely to grow. Be skeptical of an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches, duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk.\\n\\nThe sign that you skipped this is a new feature that grows an existing if/else chain by one more branch, or a second boolean that must stay in sync with the first. Temporal decomposition is another sign. Phase-named modules repeat the same domain rules across steps.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\n\\nFollow [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for source reads, writes and execution. Apply the principle within the authorized task. If writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced design proposal and state which implementation checks remain unperformed. If required domain rules or source are missing, identify them and keep the design provisional. Claim implementation or verification only for observed operations.\\n\\nPreserve explicit-invocation metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-prove-it-works\\ndescription: \\\"Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Prove It Works\\n\\nVerify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or \\\"it compiles.\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.\\n\\nCheck the real thing, not a proxy:\\n- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state\\n- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation\\n- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system\\n\\n## Script the check when you can\\n\\nThe strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.\\n\\nKeep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Run checks and retain artifacts only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. If direct inspection or execution is unavailable or denied, state which outputs remain unverified and withhold completion for those outputs. A proposed script is not evidence that it ran.\\n---\\nname: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result they observe against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns undefined, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Test Behavior, Not Implementation\\n\\nA test calls the code the way its users do and asserts the result they observe against a literal expected value. A test that asserts which calls the code made, or restates a constant the code contains, does neither.\\n\\nThe check: before you keep a test, ask whether it would still pass if every function it imports returned `undefined`. If yes, it observes no behavior and cannot fail for a defect. Rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\n\\n**Why:** A test that cannot fail for a defect costs CI time and review attention and catches nothing. A constant pin also fails when someone edits the constant or the prompt it restates, so it prevents that edit.\\n\\n**Five shapes that still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`:**\\n\\n- **Weak or no assertion.** No `expect`, or only `toBeDefined`, `toBeTruthy`, `not.toThrow`, `toBeInstanceOf`, `toBeGreaterThan(0)`.\\n- **Mock or absence only.** Only `toHaveBeenCalled`, `not.toHaveBeenCalled`, `toBeUndefined`, `toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, `not.toBe(wrongValue)`.\\n- **Self-referential.** The expected value comes from the code under test: `expect(f(a)).toBe(f(a))`, `expect(parsed.url).toBe(buildUrl(...))`.\\n- **Constant pin.** The assertion restates a hand-maintained constant, config default, table row, or prompt string: `expect(LIMITS.maxTools).toBe(8)`, `expect(PROMPT).toContain(\\\"You are\\\")`.\\n- **Fixture asserts fixture.** The assertion reads data the test built or a value computed in `beforeEach`, and the subject never runs inside the body.\\n\\n**The fix:** call the subject inside the test body with one concrete input and assert the literal output or the observable effect, `expect(slugify(\\\"Hello, World!\\\")).toBe(\\\"hello-world\\\")`. For an absence, assert the presence on the other input in the same test. For a constant, test the mechanism that reads it with one input instead of restating the value. For a mock, assert the payload it received or the state after the call, not that it was called. When no such assertion exists, delete the test.\\n\\n**Keep** a test of a relation across a table's rows (a key present in two tables, a parent that exists), and a compile-time check in a `*.test-d.ts` file.\\n\\n## Capability and permission limits\\n\\nUse [the session capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) when inspecting, changing or running tests. Work within authorized paths and permissions. If execution is unavailable or denied, provide the assertion and explain the expected empty-function failure, but report execution as unverified. Preserve `disable-model-invocation` metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: unslop\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Unslop\\n\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\n\\n## Process\\n\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\n\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\n\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\n\\n### Content\\n\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\"highlighting...\\\", \\\"ensuring...\\\", \\\"reflecting...\\\", \\\"showcasing...\\\", \\\"fostering...\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\"Experts believe\\\", \\\"Industry reports suggest\\\", \\\"Some critics argue\\\". Name the source or delete.\\n\\n### Language\\n\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\"is\\\".** \\\"serves as\\\", \\\"stands as\\\", \\\"boasts\\\", \\\"features\\\". Just say \\\"is\\\" or \\\"has\\\".\\n9. **\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\"from X to Y\\\" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\n\\n### Style\\n\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\"If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. \\\"Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English.\\\" Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.\\n15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.\\n16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: \\\"**Performance:** Performance improved...\\\". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail (\\\"**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.\\\") is fine, not a tell.\\n17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.\\n18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.\\n19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.\\n\\n### Communication artifacts\\n\\n20. **Chatbot phrases.** \\\"I hope this helps!\\\", \\\"Let me know if...\\\", \\\"Of course!\\\", \\\"Certainly!\\\", \\\"Found the smoking gun!\\\" Remove.\\n22. **Sycophantic tone.** \\\"Great question! You're absolutely right!\\\" Respond directly.\\n\\n### Filler\\n\\n23. **Filler phrases.** \\\"In order to\\\" becomes \\\"To\\\". \\\"Due to the fact that\\\" becomes \\\"Because\\\". \\\"It is important to note that\\\" gets deleted.\\n24. **Excessive hedging.** \\\"could potentially possibly be argued that it might\\\" becomes \\\"may\\\".\\n25. **Generic conclusions.** \\\"The future looks bright.\\\" State specific plans or facts.\\n\\n### Jargon\\n\\n26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in \\\"API surface\\\"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. \\\"Substrate\\\" becomes \\\"base\\\". \\\"Wedge in\\\" becomes \\\"add\\\". \\\"Vector\\\" becomes \\\"way\\\" or \\\"method\\\". \\\"Gold-plating\\\" becomes \\\"more than the job needs\\\". \\\"Ratchet\\\" becomes the mechanism's real name or \\\"a limit that only tightens\\\". \\\"Evacuate\\\" becomes \\\"move out\\\". \\\"Endgame\\\" becomes \\\"the last phase\\\". Pick the concrete word.\\n\\n### Plain speech\\n\\n27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** \\\"the database stays close at hand\\\", \\\"SQL you can read\\\", \\\"types that follow your schema\\\" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: \\\"`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database\\\", \\\"a column rename fails the build\\\". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.\\n28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.\\n29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch \\\"is/are/was/were + past participle\\\" and name the actor: \\\"queries are validated\\\" becomes \\\"the compiler validates queries\\\", \\\"the file is parsed by the loader\\\" becomes \\\"the loader parses the file\\\". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.\\n30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** \\\"runs quickly\\\" becomes \\\"is fast\\\" or the number. \\\"significantly improves\\\" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.\\n31. **Prefer the plain word.** \\\"utilize\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"leverage\\\" becomes \\\"use\\\", \\\"facilitate\\\" becomes \\\"help\\\", \\\"numerous\\\" becomes \\\"many\\\", \\\"in the event that\\\" becomes \\\"if\\\". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.\\n32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms (\\\"wire it or delete it\\\"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code (\\\"the plan holds it\\\"), figurative verbs (\\\"rides along\\\", \\\"stands on\\\"), stock framing phrases. \\\"A dial worth turning\\\" becomes \\\"a parameter worth varying\\\". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.\\n33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. \\\"Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write\\\" becomes \\\"The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing.\\\" Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\n\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\n\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\n\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\n\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\n\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\n\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only. This package writes no local custom-agent configuration and claims no current host model or worker support from that documentation.\\n# Discover capabilities in the current session\\n\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\n\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\n\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker's assigned path and permissions. |\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker's terminal state after stop. |\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\n\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\n\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\n\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\n\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\n\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\n\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e 'const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\"python3\\\",\\\"-B\\\",\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\",\\\"--root\\\",\\\".\\\",\\\"--commit\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\"1\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\n\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\n\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\n\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case's expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\n\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\n\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\n# Assignment and integration contract\\n\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\n\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers' output.\\n\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\n\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\n\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\n\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\n\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\n\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\n\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator's authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\n\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\n\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. Partition declares requiredSlices, results mapping each slice to its assignment, and gaps. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. Race declares rule, assignments, winner and ruleArtifact. first-pass must select the first completed survivor; rank-all needs all results; best-of retains an explicit reviewed selection. Cancelled assignments must be quarantined and cannot enter the aggregate. The combined partition-and-race case requires both methods and its cancellation exercise. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\n\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. Its partition-only receipt uses race null and empty cancellation, quarantine and failureExercises arrays. The combined case also records failureExercises. Each event has assignmentId, kind, attempt, order, reason and evidence, with bound result-rejection or terminal inspection. Rejected missing-revision or missing-method evidence uses attempts 0 then 1; a second invalid result exhausts the retry and leaves a failed or blocked assignment. A separate failed or blocked dropout is disclosed. These failed outputs cannot satisfy required coverage. Assign exact file paths, a named data shape and its organizing structure, and success criteria tied to the user outcome. Choose the structure before the delegate writes logic under [model-the-domain](../../principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md). Prefer a state machine over scattered booleans, a table or registry over branching, or a typed model over repeated shape assumptions. When implementation admits multiple valid shapes, such as error handling, abstraction layer or test structure, delegate through [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Its runners surface alternatives and its fresh cross-judge guards the pick. This gate is mandatory. There is no skip-with-reason escape, and Laziness Protocol does not override it. The gain is review separation, not lines saved. A worker forbidden to spawn owns the diff directly and returns it to the lead for the same review separation. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \\\"standing by\\\". Without authorized independent workers, direct implementation can be an explicit reduced result, but it does not satisfy independent review separation. The lead reviews the actual diff and owns the summary. Apply the mode's Comments rules. Make surgical edits and re-ground upstream-derived files against their source. Port shared-primitive improvements to all consumers and verify each. Commit each verified unit when authorized and after the mode's commit gates.\\n5. Retain finite guard and two decimal places. */\\\\nexport function format(n: number): string {\\\\n  // TODO: Retain existing formatting behavior and existing error type.\\\\n  throw new Error(\\\\\\\"not implemented\\\\\\\");\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\n# Module map\\\\n\\\\nThe proposed invoice.mjs remains one module with five public export names.\\\\n\\\\n- calculate owns the existing row subtotal.\\\\n- invoiceTotal privately owns discount validation and net total policy. adapter and facade are export aliases to this owner.\\\\n- controller owns response packaging and calls invoiceTotal directly.\\\\n- format owns presentation and has no callers inside the calculation path.\\\\n- readDiscount is private. Export adapter and facade as aliases to that owner, so existing named imports remain available without forwarding layers, per laziness-protocol and minimize-reader-load. controller packages the number. calculate still computes only a subtotal.\\\\n\\\\nThe invoice contains rows and one optional number. readDiscount turns omission into zero and rejects supplied nonnumeric, nonfinite, or negative values with RangeError. Model diversity remains unverified.\\\\n\\\\n## Scores\\\\n\\\\nThe parent rubric uses 0 for absent or wrong, 1 for partial, and 2 for satisfactory.\\\\n\\\\n| Criterion | A | B | Evidence |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| calculate compatibility and omitted discount | 1 | 2 | A design.ts invoiceTotal says subtract and floor unconditionally. B states it explicitly and rejects nonnumeric supplied values without coercion. |\\\\n| Clear ownership and interface depth | 2 | 2 | Each puts pricing and validation behind controller with one invoiceTotal owner. Neither requires callers to coordinate stages. |\\\\n| Caller-first usage consistent with signatures | 2 | 2 | Both include subtotal 30, discount 5, flooring, omission, zero, errors, and separate formatting with compatible types. |\\\\n| Honest risks and structural alternative | 2 | 2 | Both admit existing row and numeric behavior and compare a staged pipeline. A names removed-export risk; B names alias identity risk and also compares controller-only discount ownership. |\\\\n| Total | 8 | 10 | B wins on specified compatibility. |\\\\n\\\\n## Source check\\\\n\\\\nThe actual source is committed-inputs/shared/invoice.mjs, not invoice.mjs at repository root. The first concatenated read reported that missing root path and exited 1, while still returning all requested candidate files. A follow-up read inspected the correct source.\\\\n\\\\nSource calculate reduces qty * unitPrice from zero. adapter extracts rows, facade forwards, controller wraps the result, and format independently guards finiteness and uses toFixed(2). For rows [{qty:1,unitPrice:-5}], source calculate and controller return -5 even with discount:0. An executed Bun probe returned calculate -5, omitted total -5, zero total -5, and A's proposed unconditional floor 0. This confirms a source-compatibility issue in A's stated policy. The candidates are design sketches whose bodies throw; their runtime behavior was not executed.\\\\n\\\\nB interprets zero or omitted discount as preserving subtotal, and positive discounts as flooring subtraction at zero. This matches both the explicit compatibility requirement and the positive-discount floor requirement. Nonfinite row subtotals remain unspecified beyond preserving source behavior for zero. No new row validation should be inferred.\\\\n\\\\n## Red-flag screen\\\\n\\\\n| Flag | A | B |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| Shallow module | No blocking flag.
